records.title: Marking Contour Tones in Yorùbá: A Typographic and Computational Proposal
records.summary: Yorùbá is a tonal language in which contour tones pose persistent orthographic challenges. These are especially notable for personal names and lexical items whose conventional spellings avoid vowel lengthening that would otherwise provide a host syllable for the second tone. A particular concern is a class of names in which the conventional spelling does not just omit tonal information but inverts the meaning of said name, sometimes asserting the opposite of what the name intends. This paper describes the problem, illustrates the inadequacy of current solutions, and proposes the adoption of the caron and circumflex marks. These are symbols with precedent in Yorùbá phonological scholarship …

records.title: EpiLens: Lightweight RAG for Epidemiological Knowledge Acquisition
records.summary: To prepare for future outbreaks, researchers need to know what studies have been done and what data they use. Mapping a large literature by hand is slow, while large language models alone can misstate or conflate sources. We present EpiLens, a lightweight, open-source retrieval-augmented generation package that applies a fixed retrieval template and output schema to every paper in a corpus and links outputs to source passages. We build a corpus of 2,297 papers from the sources of a multi-pathogen parameter study and evaluate EpiLens's paper-classification workflow against 214 manually labelled papers. Without task-specific training data, the classifier matches or exceeds the tested …

records.title: Fluent but Fallible: Benchmarking Hallucination and Factual Reliability in Large Language Models
records.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced natural language processing and artificial intelligence applications through their capabilities in reasoning, text generation and knowledge retrieval. However, LLMs are still vulnerable to two important challenges: hallucination, generating factually incorrect or fabricated content, and response deviation, meaning systematic deviations from ground-truth responses. These limitations raise serious concerns regarding reliability and trustworthiness in academic and research environments. This study offers a thorough comparative analysis using a variety of metrics of ten advanced LLMs ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude~3.5~Sonnet, LLaMA~3, Mistral, …

records.title: From Solvers to Research: Large Language Model-Driven Formal Mathematics at the Research Frontier
records.summary: Recent developments in AI for Mathematics (AI4Math), especially Large Language Model (LLM)-driven theorem provers, has achieved remarkable success in formal proof generation for well-defined mathematical problems through Interactive Theorem Proving (ITP) languages. However, current systems remain fundamentally limited in tackling frontier research mathematics, such as discovering new theorems or resolving open conjectures, which are often open-ended, under-specified, and involve multiple layers of abstraction. We argue that the next leap in AI4Math systems requires a decisive shift from predefined problem-solvers to research agents that can address frontier mathematical challenges with …

records.title: HoloCosm: Beyond Single-Metric Benchmark Compression Across Multiple Metrics
records.summary: Benchmark compression reduces evaluation cost by selecting a small set of samples. Existing methods typically guide selection using a single metric, although benchmarks often assess models along multiple dimensions. We find that model rankings are often weakly correlated across metrics, indicating that different metrics capture distinct aspects of model performance. Samples selected for one metric do not reliably preserve scores and rankings on others when used for compressed evaluation. At 80\% compression, each of the five single-metric baselines yields higher reconstruction error than equal-size random sampling in over 70\% of cross-metric comparisons. To address this challenge, we …

records.title: Hierarchical Token Merging with Recursive Autoencoders for Unsupervised Grammar Induction
records.summary: Hierarchical abstraction is a fundamental principle across many data modalities, enabling complex sequences to be represented compositionally at multiple levels. Learning such hierarchies directly from data, without explicit structural supervision, remains a central challenge in representation learning. We investigate whether meaningful hierarchical structure can emerge from compression alone. While autoencoders learn compressed representations through reconstruction, this objective does not necessarily favour meaningful compositional structure. We study this challenge through unsupervised grammar induction, where the underlying hierarchy can be evaluated explicitly. We introduce a …

records.title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding
records.summary: Autoregressive language models emit one token per forward pass. This causes high inference latency, in particular as models are scaled up for quality. In this paper, we introduce Parallel Language Models (PLMs), which generate mutually consistent tokens in one forward pass by routing dependencies through latent auxiliary variables. PLMs are trained using a variational bound that reduces to an autoregressive loss plus a parallel decoding loss. Empirically, PLMs are on a faster and better Pareto frontier than autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines. Pretrained PLMs achieve near-autoregressive pretraining loss on model scales of 80M to 3B parameters, and speedup follows a power law in …

records.title: Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: Mitigating Rubric Hacking through Latent Dimension Recovery and Balancing
records.summary: Rubric hacking limits both performance and training robustness in rubric-based reinforcement learning. By decomposing rubrics into sub-dimensions, we reveal the Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: as the total rubric score increases, certain sub-dimension scores systematically decrease, suggesting the model sacrifices specific quality aspects to optimize the aggregated objective. From the sub-dimension perspective, we observe two phenomena: (1) dimension imbalance, causing the policy to favor heavily covered dimensions; (2) dimension absence, leading to a systematic gap between rewards and true quality. To mitigate these issues, we propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation (FRDA), which has …

records.title: LLM-Driven Autonomous Vehicles Can Inherit Human Driver Biases in Pedestrian Yielding: Results and Implications From a New Benchmark
records.summary: Public trust in Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) may depend not only on technical success but also on the fairness of their decision making. While a recent trend in AV research involves using general purpose "common sense" models to guide AV decision making, the degree to which these inherit human biases in driving is still understudied. Given that psychology studies have shown human driver biases exist, such as lower pedestrian-yielding rates to Black pedestrians in the US, we argue that analyses of model bias should also be part of AV evaluation. Concretely, in this paper we propose two new bias testing methodologies for Large Language Models (LLMs) and Visual-Language Models (VLMs), "All Else …

records.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows
records.summary: LLM agentic workflows increasingly employ different models for specialized roles. Users may prefer different trade-offs between task quality and deployment cost, sometimes also considering latency. Finding good assignments incurs a separate search cost from evaluating multiple candidates. We introduce Cost-Coupled Gittins (CC-Gittins), a multi-objective extension of single-objective cost-aware Gittins search for Pareto recommendation. It exploits the coupling between evaluation and deployment costs: assignments that cost more to deploy also cost more to evaluate. The search alternates between seeking higher quality and lower deployment cost, reusing each evaluation to inform both searches. …

records.title: The Development of Sycophancy in Language Models: Tracing Vulnerabilities from Pretraining to Post-Training
records.summary: Language models can change a committed answer to accommodate a user's opinion or pushback without new evidence. However, when this behaviour develops during training and what a released model inherits from earlier stages remain unclear. We follow 741 checkpoints of 30 open model lineages, from early pretraining to released models. We plant initial verdicts on moral scenarios and measure how far a model follows a user's stated opinion or abandons its verdict under pressure. In most lineages the behaviour is present before post-training, and its average strength changes in either direction, at different stages across lineages. A clearer pattern emerges at the level of individual questions. …

records.title: When the harness decides success: state that cannot be re-observed
records.summary: Agent harnesses decide what a language model sees across turns: they drop old turns, summarize them, or replay the model's own earlier reasoning. We ask when these choices change whether an agent succeeds, not only what it costs, and report three findings. First, in a pre-registered synthetic probe, truncating the context window costs a low-cost reasoning model nothing in success when a needed fact can be looked up again (it looks the fact up instead), but drops its success to chance when the fact cannot be re-observed: the two penalties differ by 92.5 percentage points (90% CI [89.5, 95.5]). A pre-registered replication on one model from a second provider showed the same contrast. Once the …

records.title: Conducting Reliable Keyword Estimation with Unreliable ASR in Police Audio Data
records.summary: Extracting insights from large audio data sets using human transcription is expensive and time-consuming. Off-the-shelf Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems offer an easy-to-use scalable alternative, but systematic transcription errors, especially in domain-specific settings, can bias downstream analyses and lead to unreliable conclusions. We investigate whether imperfect ASR transcripts can still be used to obtain statistically valid keyword frequency estimates by combining model outputs with a small set of human-labeled examples, following Prediction Powered Inference and Design-based Supervised Learning frameworks. We evaluate this approach on police radio communications from …

records.title: EngTrace: A Symbolic Benchmark for Verifiable Process Evaluation of Engineering Reasoning
records.summary: Most engineering problems involve complex multi-step derivations through checkable intermediate quantities. Grading only the final answer misjudges LLMs, crediting correct answers reached through flawed steps and penalizing wrong answers built on mostly sound ones. Yet, existing benchmarks such as SuperGPQA and EEE-Bench score only final answers, and step-level ones such as TPS-CalcBench rely on LLM judges or human graders, or cover a single domain. We therefore introduce EngTrace, a symbolic benchmark for verifiable process evaluation of engineering reasoning. Its 150 expert-certified templates, spanning five branches, 15 domains, and 42 areas, generate each problem with a gold reasoning …

records.title: BERT Is Already a Denoiser: Cheaply Unlocking Iterative Generation in Masked Language Models
records.summary: Masked language models (MLMs) such as BERT are typically used for representation learning despite their denoising pretraining. We test whether this capability supports conditional generation without diffusion training. Our decoder repeatedly predicts masked tokens and commits high-confidence predictions using a cosine schedule. It requires no diffusion timestep or reverse-diffusion objective. Frozen BERT already exhibits substantial denoising capability, reconstructing 61.0%, 37.5%, and 24.4% of masked tokens at 15%, 45%, and 60% corruption, respectively, although generation deteriorates sharply as visible context disappears. This capability alone does not yield task-directed generation: …

records.title: Teaching AI Agent to Play Poker Strategically Through Preference Optimization
records.summary: A poker agent can make a legal move and still make a strategically poor one. We ask whether compact AI agents can exhibit strategic behavior under hidden information and whether preference optimization can improve beyond static and zero-shot policies. We first evaluate a static baseline and three frozen language models: SmallThinker, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 whose performance varies substantially between exact-game and six-player evaluation. We therefore propose Strategic Preference Optimization with KL-anchored Equilibrium (SPOKE), combining teacher-relative value penalties, policy anchoring, risk constraints, and structured rationale supervision, and compare it with SFT, DPO, GRPO, and GSPO. …

records.title: PaperAudit-Bench: Benchmarking Error Detection in Research Papers for Critical Automated Peer Review
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent peer reviews but often miss sparse, subtle, and document-level scientific errors. We introduce PaperAudit-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating paper-level error detection and error-aware automated review. It comprises (1) PaperAudit-Dataset, 220 high-quality AI/ML papers containing more than 2,200 controlled synthetic errors across eight categories, and (2) PaperAudit-Review, an evidence-aware framework that links structured error detection to review generation. Experiments across models, error categories, paper sections, and analysis depths show that sparse long-context auditing remains challenging for current LLMs. Conditioning review …

records.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
records.summary: The capabilities of an agent swarm depend on both its individual members and how they coordinate. Yet existing multi-agent systems often train agents within fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior. We introduce market-based post-training (MPT), a framework for jointly learning action policies and self-orchestration in decentralized agent swarms. Agents express their willingness to participate through bids, which determine who acts and how collective outcomes provide local training credit. Learning both action and bidding behavior allows individual capabilities and patterns of participation to adapt …

records.title: From Generative to Discriminative: Lightweight Adaptation of SpeechLLMs for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
records.summary: SpeechLLMs can recognise emotion by generating a label token, but this approach relies on the LLM's existing output representations. We compare this generative approach with a discriminative alternative that uses a linear classification head on top of the LLM's hidden states. Because most multimodal emotion recognition studies evaluate with ground-truth transcripts, whereas deployed systems receive ASR output, we run every comparison with both, using a compact speechLLM (frozen Whisper-medium encoder, 3B LLM) on IEMOCAP and MELD. The classification head improves Macro F1 in 10 of 14 configurations. On IEMOCAP, it improves every configuration using ASR transcripts, reaching 76.97\% Macro F1, …

records.title: FOXGLOVE: Understanding Goal-Oriented and Anchored Writing Feedback from Experts and LLMs on Argumentative Essays
records.summary: While large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate writing feedback, there remains no systematic comparison of LLM and expert feedback on the dimensions that writing research identifies as central to revision: goal-orientation, anchoring to specific sentences, and prioritization. We introduce FOXGLOVE, a dataset of 696 feedback comments written by trained writing instructors on 69 twelfth-grade argumentative essays, paired with 1,644 comments generated from four frontier LLMs under a shared protocol, totaling 2,340 comments. We provide expert quality ratings on a subset of both instructor and LLM comments. We find that instructors and LLMs distribute feedback similarly …

records.title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement
records.summary: Drafting an answer allows a reasoning model to reconsider each decision in the context of the others. Yet repeated diffusion denoising does not ensure that individually plausible token updates form a better answer together. We introduce Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLMs), which use a single denoiser to propose parallel revisions and evaluate a candidate draft. We train the denoiser to reconstruct every token from uniformly corrupted drafts, teaching both preservation and repair. Its predictions specify revisions directly, without a diffusion reverse transition. Evaluation requires a different use of these predictions: confidence in an existing token reflects both contextual support …

records.title: ReAnchor: Reusing Rejected Verifier States for Diffusion Drafting
records.summary: Block diffusion drafters accelerate speculative decoding by generating multiple draft tokens in a single forward pass. However, each pass produces only a fixed-length block from a single target-generated anchor, limiting how far the draft can extend. Meanwhile, target verification computes hidden states even at positions beyond the first rejection, but these states are typically discarded rather than reused. We propose ReAnchor, a training-free method that reanchors a pretrained drafter at shifted positions using discarded verifier states to generate parallel draft blocks. These blocks improve predictions within the original block and extend coverage beyond its endpoint. At sampling …

records.title: A Fisher-Geometric View of Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
records.summary: Consolidating specialized foundation models into a unified generalist is a central goal of post-training. Two approaches are in common use: model merging, which is fast but treated as a heuristic, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation, which matches distributions but demands heavy rollout compute and suffers from cross-task gradient conflict. We show that the two are one objective seen at different orders. Within a shared basin of homologous specialists, the multi-teacher on-policy distillation objective is, to second order, exactly the Fisher-merging objective. Its minimizer is therefore the Fisher merge, a classic model-merging method given by a closed-form combination of the …

records.title: Move by Move: Measuring and Steering How LLMs Conduct Psychotherapy
records.summary: As the demand for mental health services outpaces clinical workforce capacity, users are increasingly turning to large language models (LLMs) for accessible and private support. Although recent evaluations suggest LLM care can reduce clinical symptoms, how models actually conduct therapeutic interactions compared to trained human clinicians remains largely unknown. Drawing on established clinical psychology frameworks that conceptualize therapy as a sequential decision-making process, we can systematically analyze the conversational interventions used in AI-driven sessions. To achieve this, we introduce an original, clinically validated ontology of ten distinct therapeutic moves to …

records.title: RouterWorld: Scaling Conversational AI with Latency-Aware LLM Routing
records.summary: Conversational AI systems built on Large Language Models (LLMs) require routing mechanisms that balance answer quality and response latency at scale. However, existing LLM routing benchmarks assume full observability of all candidate model outcomes, under-emphasize latency as a first-class metric, and fragment evaluation across heterogeneous protocols misaligned with real-world settings. We introduce RouterWorld, a comprehensive benchmark for LLM routing in conversational GenAI. RouterWorld unifies 371k single-turn responses and 76k multi-turn agentic trajectories, adopts natural user interactions with a standardized LLM-as-a-judge protocol, and decouples efficiency from transient pricing …

records.title: Multilingual Reasoning Cascades Need More Context
records.summary: Translation cascades for reasoning translate the query from another language to English, reason in English, and translate the answer back to the original language. This is a competitive approach to multilingual reasoning, but structurally lossy, since each stage discards information later stages may need, including cues for cultural grounding, register, and disambiguation. We examine the benefits of a simple and training-free intervention: a context-aware translation cascade, which additionally provides the original question, the English translated question, and the reasoning trace to the context of the final translation module. We evaluate gains across nine multilingual benchmarks …

records.title: User Model Extraction via Belief Self-Distillation
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) implicitly infer attributes of their users and adapt their behavior accordingly, yet these beliefs remain difficult to inspect and causally manipulate. We introduce Belief Self-Distillation (BSD), a unified read-write framework that bridges linear and causal probing by learning a compact user representation that can be both decoded and written back into the model. The frozen LLM acts as its own teacher, distilling beliefs from natural conversations without external annotations. Unlike conventional probing, BSD isolates not only information present in activations, but a state whose causal role can be directly tested. Across multiple model families, BSD faithfully …

records.title: Strength Controls Change How Interventions Compare Across Sparse Autoencoder Codes
records.summary: Changing sparse autoencoder (SAE) codes can alter both intervention direction and magnitude, so comparing intervention effects requires a strength control specifying what is held equal. Norm matching and output calibration provide different controls, but whether interventions yield different effects across codes after strength matching remains unclear. We compare intervention effects under these controls for fixed feature groups in Gemma and Llama and observe: (1) Whole-patch scaling. With one coefficient per input, full-output Kullback-Leibler (KL) calibration leaves smaller mean effect gaps from the encoder-based reference intervention than total-norm matching for nonnegative …

records.title: Agent-OM: Leveraging LLM Agents for Ontology Matching
records.summary: Ontology matching (OM) enables semantic interoperability between different ontologies and resolves their conceptual heterogeneity by aligning related entities. OM systems currently have two prevailing design paradigms: conventional knowledge-based expert systems and newer machine learning-based predictive systems. While large language models (LLMs) and LLM agents have revolutionised data engineering and have been applied creatively in many domains, their potential for OM remains underexplored. This study introduces a novel agent-powered LLM-based design paradigm for OM systems. With consideration of several specific challenges in leveraging LLM agents for OM, we propose a generic framework, …

records.title: 'Your AI Text is not Mine': Redefining and Evaluating AI-generated Text Detection under Realistic Assumptions
records.summary: Although it is generally agreed that AI-generated text poses a broad societal risk, there is no common understanding in the AI-generated text detection literature on what constitutes harmful use. Rather, existing datasets and approaches often define their own criteria and make their own assumptions, sometimes implicitly, and often only loosely related to real-world needs and applications. To address this gap, we here systematically define various notions of AI-generated text and their characteristics. To study these, we collect AITDNA - a new benchmark of human-machine co-constructed texts that is annotated with detailed genesis information, such as the entire edit and AI-interaction …

records.title: Training Negatives Still Matter After Calibrating Answerability Readouts
records.summary: Answerability readouts predict whether a passage supplies an answer, but whether calibration can compensate for removing negative passages during training remains unclear. We present a controlled study of how training-negative construction affects calibrated prediction, ranking, and downstream answer retention. We compare native training, which retains negative passages, with empty training, which removes them, holding questions, labels, positive examples, and model weights fixed. Both are calibrated on the same labeled native examples. On SQuAD 2.0 and RepLiQA, native-trained logistic readouts at selected depths achieve lower Brier loss for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-it, with or …

records.title: Iterate Until Retrieved: Factual Nugget Optimization for Discoverable Continual Corrections in Agentic RAG
records.summary: Agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in business-to-business settings may often receive free-form response feedback. Rather than generic feedback signals such as style, preference, or overall response quality, we focus on actionable factual corrections. We identify these instances and convert them into compact knowledge-base entries, which we call factual nuggets. We introduce Iterative Nugget Optimization (INO), an index-time optimization method that uses the production agentic RAG as a test harness: it creates an initial nugget, probes it with the triggering query and paraphrases, reflects over failed retrieval and answer traces, and revises the nugget until it is …

records.title: TeleASR-Amharic: A Benchmark for Robust Amharic ASR in Realistic Telecommunication Conditions
records.summary: The real-world usability of ASR models remains challenging, particularly for low-resource languages, where existing speech resources are often collected in clean studio environments. In this work, we introduce TeleASR-Amharic, a benchmark for evaluating Amharic ASR under various acoustic and telecommunication conditions. We analyze the major degradations observed in real telecommunications recordings and develop a benchmark that covers multiple channel conditions, environmental disturbances, and telecom-domain variations. Our results show that telecommunication degradation can substantially reduce recognition performance, making even high-performing ASR models impractical under severe …

records.title: Label Authority in Speech Emotion Recognition: Intended and Perceived Ground Truth in Emozionalmente
records.summary: Ground truth in Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is often presented as a single categorical fact, yet an acted emotion and the emotion heard by listeners describe different aspects of the same recording. We examine this distinction in Emozionalmente, an acted Italian corpus that provides both an elicited production label and five listener judgements for every clip. Using frozen XLS-R, HuBERT, and WavLM representations with matched probes, we compare three label authorities: the expressed condition, the listeners' hard plurality, and their complete vote distribution. The results tell a consistent story. Recovering the expressed condition is easier than predicting a tie-broken listener …

records.title: WenSight-Decision-1 for Direct Decisions under E-commerce Rules
records.summary: E-commerce decisions require applying natural-language rules to the available case evidence. We introduce WenSight-Decision-1, a shared model that scores supplied options directly from rules and case information for six operational tasks, with examples spanning six languages. We fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B with reference options as supervision, using the same option scores for training and inference. On 1,440 synthetic operational cases reserved for final evaluation, accuracy rises from 61.60% for Qwen3.5-9B to 92.92% for WenSight-Decision-1 under identical inputs and scoring. Joint fine-tuning improves all six tasks, bringing heterogeneous operational judgments under a common decision interface.

records.title: The Geometry of Agent Memory: Forecasting Retrieval-Bound Memory Failures, and Characterizing Its Limits
records.summary: We study whether geometric relationships between conversation turns, memory texts, and queries can predict answer correctness before generation. We evaluate four memory implementations with dense or hybrid retrieval and one observation-summary comparator. We embed these texts in a shared space. A logistic classifier uses 25 features describing query proximity, memory-conversation correspondence, and conversation structure. On LongMemEval-small, pooled AUROC is 0.640 over 2,367 question-system pairs, below a question-difficulty baseline of 0.655. Performance varies by question type: geometry reaches 0.841 on single-session-assistant questions, but system identity alone reaches 0.826. After …

records.title: HarnessRL: Co-Evolving Policies with a Just-in-Time Training Harness for Open-Ended RL
records.summary: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) trains policies for open-ended generation with natural-language criteria as rewards, but these rewards can become ineffective as training progresses. We identify two failure modes. Under non-discriminative rewards, scores collapse to uniformly low or high values due to insufficient exploration or a mismatch between task difficulty and policy capability. Under spurious rewards, higher scores do not correspond to better responses. Both reflect a training configuration whose task sampling, exploration, and evaluation stay fixed as the policy evolves. We introduce HarnessRL, a training-time harness that co-evolves with the policy through three interfaces …

records.title: SNO-PI: Label-Scarce SNOMED CT Entity Linking with Pre-trained Encoders and Curated Terminology Knowledge
records.summary: We present SNO-PI, the top-performing submission on SNOMED International's SNOMED CT Entity Linking Benchmark as of 18 October 2026. SNO-PI achieves a macro character IoU of 0.5387, outperforming the organisers' reference system (0.4582; based on the 2024 challenge winner's approach) by 18% relative. Linking clinical mentions to SNOMED CT is a zero- and few-shot problem over a very large label space: the 272 annotated MIMIC-IV discharge summaries cover only 6,595 of the roughly 219,000 eligible concepts, and a third of those occur only once. This motivates a design built on transfer from pre-trained models and human-curated knowledge. SNO-PI combines high-recall span proposal, SapBERT …

records.title: Governing the Rule Space. Ruliology, Computational Irreducibility and Anticipatory Governance of Quantum Technologies
records.summary: The regulation of emerging technologies is often conceived as a strategy of catching up, because legislators arrive too late. Yet gathering signals, constructing scenarios and adapting rules to an anticipated future are fundamental tasks for those entrusted with governance, including the governance of rules themselves. The literature on so-called future law has already shown that anticipation means building institutional capabilities rather than predicting outcomes precisely (anticipatory governance). Taking this premise as its starting point, this article proposes to understand regulation as an exploration of the transformations that may occur. The Ruliological Framework for Anticipatory …

records.title: Self-Consistency of Entity Sets and Citations in a Deep Research System under Repeated Prompting
records.summary: Deep research agents (DRA) are commonly used for open-ended synthesis tasks where closed-world QA benchmarks are poorly suited to characterize relevant aspects of performance. We study the self-consistency of one commercial deep research system under repeated identical prompting, representing each report with the set of named entities it mentions, categorised by a custom schema, and the set of citations it retrieves. Across repeated runs of a single open-ended cybersecurity related prompt, we quantify pairwise overlap to characterize how stable the retrieved and synthesized output structure is under repeated identical prompts. In ten runs, the pairwise entity Jaccard results in a median of …

records.title: Co-Evolving Policy and Reward for Code Generation: A Mechanistic Study of Single-Adapter Drift
records.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is particularly well suited to code generation because generated programs can be objectively evaluated through execution. Execution also provides behavioral information that can be reused as additional supervision. The Synergistic Policy and Reward Co-Evolving Framework (SPARK), originally proposed for reasoning tasks, exploits this idea by recycling training rollouts and their evaluation results to train a model not only to generate solutions but also to evaluate and improve them. records.title: Where Does Rhetorical Distortion Live? A Multi-Platform, Multi-Language Measurement of Influencer Content
records.summary: Much of the manipulation in online influencer content is not false but disproportionate: an accurate fact is framed as historic, urgent, or catastrophic. Fact-checking and clickbait detection are not designed to capture such framing, and little is known about where it originates: with the creator, the topic, the platform, or the audience that replies. records.title: Expert L2 English Speech Evaluation on a Gaming PC: Accuracy, Fluency, and Prosody with XLS-R, XEUS, and PhoneticXeus
records.summary: oollim is a locally executable system for evaluating L2 English pronunciation accuracy, fluency, and prosody on a consumer computer. The system combines pretrained XLS-R, XEUS, and PhoneticXeus representations with reference-text features and ridge regressions trained on SpeechOcean762, the Korean Learners' L2 Speech Corpus (English), J-AESOP, and their combinations. records.title: LaMER: Language-Conditioned Multi-Expert Routing for Weakly Supervised Referring Expression Comprehension
records.summary: Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) localizes the image region described by a natural language expression, underpinning applications such as autonomous navigation, human-robot interaction, and medical image analysis. Under weak supervision, REC is challenged by the visual-linguistic semantic gap and the difficulty of inferring region-text correspondences from coarse image-level signals alone. Moreover, no single visual encoder captures all complementary properties---semantic alignment, fine-grained texture, and boundary awareness---while naively fusing multiple pretrained encoders yields heterogeneous, hard-to-reconcile representations. records.title: How Benchmark Graph Construction Shapes Multi-Hop KG Navigation: A Controlled Audit of PathQuestion and PathQuestion-Large
records.summary: Multi-hop knowledge-graph question answering (KGQA) benchmarks are often treated as fixed language-and-reasoning tasks, but for navigation-based methods, difficulty also depends on the graph in which those tasks are instantiated. This makes graph construction a consequential but often entangled part of the navigation task. To isolate this effect, we audit PathQuestion (PQ) and PathQuestion-Large (PQL) as graph-navigation benchmarks under a controlled intervention: we hold questions, topic entities, released answers, released path annotations, and family-level splits fixed while replacing each released task-filtered graph with the larger source KG distributed with the benchmark. records.title: Leveraging Low-Level Symbolic Competences for Unsupervised Grounding in Hallucination Detection
records.summary: Hallucination-where a language model generates outputs that are factually incorrect or unsupported by the source-is a major challenge for both prompted and fine-tuned language models. Detecting hallucinations is difficult due to the opaque reasoning processes of LLMs, which often provide little insight into why a model's output may be inaccurate. In this work, we investigate whether an LLM can use an alternative, low level, symbolic competence such as SQL for unsupervised hallucination detection in some high level task. records.title: Bridged Self-Distillation for On-Policy Learning
records.summary: On-policy distillation can transfer the reasoning capabilities of a strong teacher to a smaller student. However, distillation from a stronger teacher model faces two mismatches: its solutions may be difficult for a smaller student to imitate, and its token-level probabilities may be incompatible with, or even unavailable to, the student. Existing methods handle these settings through different forms of supervision. To this end, we propose Bridged Self-Distillation (BSD), a unified framework for distilling from any teacher that provides reasoning traces. records.title: Dissecting Training-Free Uncertainty Estimation in Multimodal Large Language Models
records.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical settings, yet estimating when their answers can be trusted remains underexplored. We systematically compare training-free verbalized, token-level and semantic uncertainty estimation methods on twelve MLLMs and five VQA benchmarks. We find that answer length decides which family wins: token-level entropy on short answers, verbalized methods on sentence-length responses, and semantic methods on long-form generation. Token-level entropy becomes far more informative when estimated at a higher temperature than the low ones used to generate answers, and asking a model to judge its own answer becomes more …

records.title: An Empirical Study of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
records.summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods are critical for adapting large models under resource-constrained settings. However, as mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures, which offer efficient inference at massive parameter scales, gain increasing prevalence in the community, a critical gap arising from the lack of systematic recipes for applying PEFT to MoE models. To narrow this gap, we conduct a large-scale systematic study that investigates a set of essential design recipes, including which modules should be adapted, which granularity should be used to adapt MoE modules, which PEFT method to use, and to what extent should the load-balancing objective be used, across three MoE …

records.title: QuasiLeak-Bench: Evaluating LLM-Based Privacy Detectors on Policy-Conditioned Quasi-Evidence Group Recovery
records.summary: Natural language messages often contain quasi-identifiers that are weak in isolation but can jointly reveal an individual's private attributes. We call such a jointly revealing set of cues a quasi-evidence group. Existing privacy benchmarks focus on explicit identifiers, attribute inference, or task-driven disclosures, leaving inference from quasi-evidence groups largely unmeasured. In practice, whether exposing such a quasi-evidence group violates privacy also depends on sender-specified disclosure policies. We introduce QuasiLeak-Bench, a benchmark for policy-conditioned quasi-evidence group recovery, which evaluates whether detectors recover complete quasi-evidence groups and flag the …

records.title: AD4EDU: Benchmarking University Lecture Audio Description across Accessibility Standards, Metrics, and Learner Preferences
records.summary: Audio description (AD) aims to enhance the accessibility of visual media for blind and low-vision (BLV) persons. However, in higher education, where slide-based lectures are a default mode of teaching, lecture AD remains largely underexplored. The main reason is that existing production guidelines, evaluation metrics, and benchmark datasets are oriented toward entertainment content and do not transfer to lectures, where ADs must complement the lecturer's speech, resolve deictic references, and fit within narrow pauses. In this work, we propose AD4Edu, consisting of an AD benchmark, AD4Edu-Bench, and a rule-diagnosable evaluation metric, AD4Edu-Eval, for generating and evaluating ADs in …

records.title: UZHCL_for_the_win at Touche: Encoder Fine-Tuning, Synthetic Augmentation, and an Underpowered Encoder-LLM Comparison
records.summary: Online discussions on platforms like Reddit are a productive testbed for fallacy detection: short texts, broad topical range, and the full inventory of informal fallacies. The Touche 2026 lab at CLEF formalises this as a shared task on a Reddit-derived corpus that combines fallacy detection with argument-scheme classification. This paper describes our participation in all three subtasks (ST1 binary fallacy detection, ST2 eight-way fallacy classification, ST3 four-way argument-scheme classification) and both evaluation tracks. Our submitted systems are fine-tuned RoBERTa-large encoders with task-specific heads, augmented with a small batch of LLM-generated synthetic contrastive pairs; for …

records.title: Large-Scale Biomedical RAG: Corpus Scaling, Document Representation, and Efficiency Trade-offs
records.summary: We present a controlled, large-scale evaluation of how corpus scale, document representation, and reranking affect the effectiveness and efficiency of biomedical Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. Retrieval collections were progressively expanded while retaining the relevant source documents, enabling consistent comparisons across corpus sizes. We compared abstract, flat full-text, and hierarchical full-text representations across first-stage retrieval, reranking, and end-to-end multiple-choice question answering. Configurations selected on development data were evaluated on five external biomedical benchmarks and a held-out test set, while retrieval latency and index storage …

records.title: Typed Decision Models under Prevalence Shift: Decision Training, Calibration, and Implicit Priors
records.summary: Typed decision models (TDMs) return a probability over caller-defined options, and Jev is described by its vendor as calibrated. But in deployment class frequencies change, so calibration measured on a fixed test set need not hold where thresholds are applied. Existing evaluations leave two gaps: the gains of vendor decision training have not been separated from those of the backbone under an identical readout, and TDMs have been tested only at the test set's class distribution. We ask whether decision training improves a model over its own backbone, and whether a TDM's calibration and thresholds withstand prevalence (label) shift as well as a fine-tuned classifier's. records.title: The Scheduler Is a Hidden Retriever: How Asynchrony Shapes Evidence Acquisition in Search Agents
records.summary: Language-model agents increasingly solve complex tasks through parallel reasoning and asynchronous information gathering. Controlled replay across two model families and three benchmarks shows that delivery timing redirects search decisions made before all results arrive, despite identical initial evidence. Acquisition disagreement reaches up to 24 percentage points above same-order repeat variation. This dependence persists after all initial evidence arrives and through a second search, turning temporary differences in what agents have seen into lasting differences in what they acquire. An acquisition-regret bound with a matching construction shows that invariance at a fixed early arrival …

records.title: Answering While You Type: Optimizing Time-to-Answer with Streaming Generation
records.summary: Work on efficient large-language-model inference has concentrated almost entirely on reducing the cost of decoding once a request is complete. The quantity a user experiences, however, is the interval between submitting a request and receiving a usable response, and that interval can be shortened without making decoding itself faster. While a request is being composed it is already partially specified, yet conventional deployments begin no computation until submission. We propose and study streaming generation, a decoding regime in which the model begins producing a response from an incomplete request and revises it as the remaining input arrives, so that only a small residue of the answer …

records.title: OM4OV: Leveraging Ontology Matching for Ontology Versioning
records.summary: Due to the dynamics of the Semantic Web, version control is necessary to manage changes in widely used ontologies. Despite the long-standing recognition of ontology versioning (OV) as a crucial component of efficient ontology management, many approaches treat OV as similar to ontology matching (OM) and directly reuse OM systems for OV tasks. In this study, we systematically analyse similarities and differences between OM and OV and formalise an OM4OV framework to offer more advanced OV support. The framework is implemented and evaluated in the state-of-the-art OM system Agent-OM. The experimental results indicate that OM systems can be effectively reused for OV tasks, but without the …

records.title: Steering Language Models Before They Speak: Logit-Level Interventions
records.summary: Controllable generation requires language models to realize output characteristics such as reading level, politeness, and toxicity. Existing steering methods are often indirect, require access to internal activations, or depend on auxiliary trained models. We propose SWAI, a training-free inference-time method that addresses these limitations by steering directly in logit space using corpus-derived token statistics. SWAI computes z-normalized one-vs-rest log-odds scores from labeled corpora and biases high-scoring tokens only within the model's top-K candidate set, allowing control to favor target-characteristic tokens while preserving contextually plausible choices. records.title: Decomposed Relation Extraction from Aviation Accident Narratives: Evaluating Transformer-Based Safety Knowledge Discovery under Relational Sparsity
records.summary: Relation extraction from aviation accident narratives is challenging because genuine safety relations are sparse among possible concept pairs. This study evaluates a decomposed framework separating relation classification from concept identification. A benchmark of 300 National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) narratives containing 2,524 unique concept-text nodes was expanded into 21,038 ordered candidate pairs, with only 248 (1.18%) representing RESULTS_IN or CONTRIBUTES_TO relations. A TF-IDF Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) and weighted RoBERTa classifier were developed using an independent graph-annotated resource with hard-negative sampling and frozen before sealed evaluation. …

records.title: VLX-Go: Robust Embodied Tracking through Multi-Stage Learning and On-Policy Refinement
records.summary: Embodied visual tracking requires a robot to identify a designated target from visual observations and control its own motion to follow that target through an environment. Following an isolated person is a comparatively simple demonstration of embodied visual tracking, but following the intended person among distractors remains challenging. Existing methods exhibit a substantial drop in success from single-target to distractor tracking, motivating a focus on the shared spaces that person-following robots must navigate. We present VLX-GO, a vision-language waypoint policy built around the hypothesis that visual and language representations should be aligned before tracking-specific motion is …

records.title: AutoMind: Adaptive Knowledgeable Agent for Automated Data Science
records.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have shown great potential in addressing real-world data science problems. LLM-driven data science agents promise to automate the entire machine learning pipeline, yet their real-world effectiveness remains limited. Existing frameworks depend on rigid, pre-defined workflows and inflexible coding strategies; consequently, they excel only on relatively simple, classical problems and fail to capture the empirical expertise that human practitioners bring to complex, innovative tasks. In this work, we introduce AutoMind, an adaptive, knowledgeable LLM-agent framework that overcomes these deficiencies through three key advances: (1) a curated expert knowledge …

records.title: AudioScorer: Learning Question-Aware Token Relevance for Large Audio Language Models
records.summary: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) reason over speech, environmental sounds, music, and other acoustic information. However, their audio encoders produce dense token sequences that make long-form audio costly to process. Existing audio pruning methods reduce this cost using heuristics such as attention, representation similarity, or temporal sampling, but do not explicitly learn which tokens are most useful for a given question. We propose AudioScorer, a lightweight model that scores audio tokens according to the user question. It is trained by distilling the ranking of audio tokens under the frozen LALM's answer-gradient saliency, together with downstream answer supervision. Compared with …

records.title: Machina Pauliana: A neuro-symbolic approach to the actio pauliana in Dutch insolvency law
records.summary: Applying a legal provision frequently requires both structured rule-based reasoning and sensitivity to open-textured terms developed in case law. The actio pauliana of Article 42 of the Dutch Bankruptcy Act (Faillissementswet, Fw), which allows an insolvency practitioner to avoid transactions that prejudice creditors, requires both. We present a neuro-symbolic model of Article 42 Fw. Its symbolic core is written in Catala in a literate style that keeps statute and formalisation aligned and was developed through pair programming, with open-textured terms represented as boolean inputs where neural components couple to the symbolic solver. records.title: Shaping the Document, Not the Model: Optimized Suffixes for Context Following
records.summary: When a user supplies a document and wants the answer drawn from it, a language model is expected to follow it even when it contradicts its parametric knowledge. Prior work has focused on making the model rely on context by steering activations, contrasting logits during decoding, or instructing it in plain language. We ask whether the document alone, with no instruction written into it and no access to the model at inference time, is enough. We optimize a document suffix by discrete token search, starting from the answer to a single question and extending the objective to a set of passages, to multi-hop questions that follow from the planted fact, and to later turns of a conversation. records.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
records.summary: Tool-using voice agents often leave users waiting after speech ends, even when actionable information arrives earlier in the request. Speculative approaches begin work during speech, but chunk-bounded or interrupt-on-update generation can truncate a tool call before its arguments are complete. This couples computation time to speech updates, limiting useful work completed in advance. We introduce Heartbeat Thinking, which handles updated input through new Thinker invocations while allowing ongoing invocations and dispatched tools to finish. records.title: Rethinking BPE: Merge Selection as Model Selection
records.summary: Subword tokenization methods such as Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) are a core component of modern language models; yet, tokenizer capacity remains typically determined by a fixed merge budget, chosen heuristically. Since larger vocabularies increase memory usage and computational cost, selecting compact and effective token inventories is essential for efficient language modeling. We study the optimization of a BPE merge budget as a statistical model selection problem and investigate information-theoretic criteria for \emph{computing optimal merge sets} directly from corpus statistics. records.title: RLTLDR: Self-improvement by Internalizing Self-generated Feedback
records.summary: The common paradigm of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is to let agents make multiple attempts at a task, and optimize towards the successful ones. This becomes problematic in the realms of self-improvement, where tasks are so difficult that the agent has a low or even no chance of success, and where there are no teacher models or example solutions to distill from. In this paper, we introduce RLTLDR. After each failed attempt, we show the policy the verifier outputs and let it write its own feedback, in the form of a single TL;DR insight. The next rollout is conditioned on all previous insights, and we sequentially sample rollouts until a solution is found. Moreover, …

records.title: Open-sci-ref-0.02: open reference baselines for reproducible language model and dataset comparison
records.summary: Reliable progress in language modeling depends on knowing whether a new dataset, architecture, or training recipe is genuinely better than existing alternatives. To foster reproducible learning procedure comparison, we present open-sci-ref, a family of dense transformers trained as open reference baselines at four scales (0.13B-1.7B parameters) on nine main reference datasets, with token budgets up to 1T, using a single tuned and fully documented training procedure. To facilitate a shared experimentation and measurement infrastructure, we release model weights, intermediate checkpoints, training logs, code, and downstream evaluations. When comparing training procedures, we take into account …

records.title: Reading Time Modeling with Pixel-Based Language Models
records.summary: Tokenization-free, pixel-based language models (PLMs) have recently been proposed as an alternative to conventional token-based language models (TLMs), typically motivated by practical considerations, e.g., the flexibility to support new languages or vocabularies. Nevertheless, PLMs also have the potential to serve as infrastructure for computational (psycho)linguistics, where tokenization has been a source of bias in estimating information-theoretic values, such as surprisal, and has pushed the bottom-up visual orthographic features outside the scope. In this study, we first integrate PLMs into the modeling of naturalistic human reading and, in particular, examine their use to estimate …

records.title: Conditional information Retrieval for Longitudinal Survey Harmonisation
records.summary: Identifying conceptually equivalent questions across different surveys is a challenging information retrieval task where surface-level textual similarity is insufficient. Two questions may be lexically similar yet assess entirely different sociological sub-concepts, or lexically different yet conceptually equivalent. We introduce a conditional information retrieval framework that addresses this by decomposing the task into two steps: concept extraction, which identifies the underlying sociological concept of a survey question using a fine-tuned generative model, and concept-aware retrieval, which augments question representations with the extracted concept as an explicit conditioning signal …

records.title: VISAGENT: An Agent-Based End-to-End Voice Interaction System
records.summary: Voice-based public services have evolved from manual switchboards to intelligent platforms to meet modern user needs. However, current systems remain constrained by rigid menu-driven interaction, fragmented vertical services, and limited extensibility. To address these issues, we present VISAGENT, an agent-based end-to-end voice interaction system for large-scale public services that integrates end-to-end speech interaction, hierarchical agent routing, a scalable voice-agent marketplace, and user memory support. records.title: Annotrace: A Workbench for Step-Level Annotation of Agent Traces
records.summary: Every study of why LLM agents fail begins by labelling traces by hand, and every such study builds its own throwaway tool. Observability platforms record agent traces but offer no structured labelling; annotation tools label text but have no notion of a step, a delegation or a tool call, leaving it unclear what the smallest unit of execution to label should be. Annotrace reads six trace formats, including OpenTelemetry GenAI, LangSmith and Langfuse, and turns each run into an ordered, nested list of steps. records.title: DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia
records.summary: While language models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities, their performance remains disproportionately skewed towards high-resource languages. This disparity is particularly acute for the 700 million inhabitants of Southeast Asia, where vast linguistic diversity remains under-represented in existing benchmarks, often suffering from limited language coverage or narrow task scopes. To address this, we introduce DeepSEA, a comprehensive benchmark constructed from established datasets through professional human translation into 12 Southeast Asian languages, spanning both high-resource (e.g., Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese) and low-resource (e.g., Burmese, Khmer, Lao) tiers across five …

records.title: Brain-to-Language Decoding: Paradigms, Signals, Methods, Evaluation, Practical Use and Beyond
records.summary: Brain-to-language decoding translates neural activity associated with language production, internal speech and perception into linguistic or expressive outputs. It offers a route to restoring communication after speech loss and a means of studying how the brain represents language. Advances in neural recording and representation learning have expanded the field from constrained recognition and acoustic reconstruction to text generation, streaming personalised speech and facial animation. This survey synthesises these developments across invasive and non-invasive measurements. We connect Articulated, Inner and Perceived paradigms to the neural populations they engage, the representations …

records.title: VLegal-Bench: Cognitively Grounded Benchmark for Vietnamese Legal Reasoning of Large Language Models
records.summary: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has enabled new possibilities for applying artificial intelligence within the legal domain. Nonetheless, the complexity, hierarchical organization, and frequent revisions of Vietnamese legislation pose considerable challenges for evaluating how well these models interpret and utilize legal knowledge. To address this gap, the Vietnamese Legal Benchmark (VLegal-Bench) is introduced, the first comprehensive benchmark designed to systematically assess LLMs on Vietnamese legal tasks. Informed by Bloom's cognitive taxonomy, VLegal-Bench encompasses multiple levels of legal understanding through tasks designed to reflect practical usage …

records.title: Language steering in latent space to mitigate unintended code-switching
records.summary: Multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) often exhibit hallucinations such as unintended code-switching, reducing reliability in downstream tasks. We propose latent-space language steering, a lightweight inference-time method that identifies language directions via Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on parallel translations and steers token embeddings along these axes to control language identity. Our approach mitigates code-switching (reduced next-token distributional divergence by up to 55\%, reduced Code-Switching Index by 63--99\%) while preserving broad semantic direction with negligible computational overhead and requires only minimal parallel data for calibration. records.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
records.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in scientific research aims to improve agents' research capabilities through their own experimental experience. Scientific agent swarms can combine evidence and implementations from different research directions to guide their agents' subsequent experiments. However, poor experimental results can leave unclear whether to revise a hypothesis or its implementation, while overall program scores can hide components useful to other agents. To address these challenges, we introduce SwarmRSI, a framework that evolves scientific agent swarms for recursive self-improvement. We devise Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation to refine hypotheses and their implementations using …

records.title: Evaluating Tibetan Speech Recognition Across Dialects and Adaptation Regimes: A Multi-Granularity Analysis
records.summary: Tibetan speech recognition is usually evaluated with character or syllable error rates because the writing system does not mark word boundaries. These metrics can rank systems differently and respond differently to adaptation failures. We combine character error rate, syllable error rate, and segmented word error rate in one evaluation framework. We use dictionary-based, neural, and language-model-based segmentation and compare their boundaries with expert annotations. We evaluate five ASR architectures on Lhasa Tibetan, then test zero-shot transfer and target-corpus adaptation on five additional corpus subsets. We also vary LoRA rank and training-data size to examine adaptation failure. …

records.title: CompactAttention: Accelerating Chunked Prefill with Block-Union KV Selection
records.summary: Chunked prefill has become a widely adopted serving strategy for long-context large language models, but efficient attention computation in this regime remains challenging. Existing sparse attention methods are primarily designed for one-shot prefill and do not translate efficiently to chunked prefill: block-sparse kernels lose efficiency when the query length is limited by the chunk size, while fine-grained pattern search becomes costly when repeated over the accumulated KV cache at every chunk. QUOKA, a recent method that directly targets chunked prefill, avoids sparse-kernel overhead but relies on query-subsampled, token-level KV selection, which can miss query-specific KV entries and …

records.title: Honeyed Words, Hidden Daggers: Benchmarking and Training LLMs to See Through Mock Politeness
records.summary: The Chinese idiom "kou mi fu jian" ("honeyed words, hidden daggers") names speech that is polite in form but hostile in function. We present ZhenhuanBench, a 1,592-item benchmark built from expert commentary on Empresses in the Palace, covering speaker intent, emotion-language mismatch, and per-listener uptake. Text-only evaluation covers 34 LLMs. GPT-6 Astra leads the leaderboard at 73.48% overall, while its listener-reaction score is 58.37%. The annotations also supply supervised traces and string-verifiable training rewards. With 338 gold traces, an 8B model outperforms teacher distillation on identical items. records.title: Balance-Aware Pivot Selection for Parallel Diffusion LLM Decoding
records.summary: Diffusion language models enable parallel token generation, offering a promising alternative to sequential autoregressive decoding. Existing acceleration methods use predictive confidence to enable parallel token commitment while preserving generation quality. However, confidence-based selection prioritizes reliable token predictions without explicitly considering how token positions shape the remaining decoding schedule. Moreover, such ordering does not always reflect inter-token dependencies, suggesting that confidence need not be the sole criterion for token selection. records.title: Decision4Rec: A Jev-Inspired Framework of Decision Models on Knowledge and Active Graphs for Multi-Agent Recommender Systems
records.summary: Decision models, such as the commercial Jev, are language models that return one probability for each option of a question instead of generating text. We present Decision4Rec, an open and modular framework that makes decision models useful for recommendation. A knowledge graph writes the logs of each recommendation scenario as short statements on a defined scale, such as "sold: top 10%". A pool of agents, proposes candidates, and a residual ranker keeps the best 30. A decision model, trained once on real choices of three scenarios, reads them through one interface of typed questions, and a fusion step combines its answers with the score of the ranker. Any model with this interface can be …

records.title: Understanding When Reflective Prompt and Skill Optimization Helps on Locally Served Reasoning Models: A Two-Model Study of GEPA and SkillOpt
records.summary: Reflective text-space optimizers such as GEPA and SkillOpt have reported large gains on frontier and mid-size models. We test replication across two reasoning-native target-serving configurations: DeepSeek V4 Flash through DwarfStar and Qwen3.8-27B through LM Studio. For each target, we evaluate the same held-out tasks and four conditions - minimal baseline, GEPA prompt, SkillOpt skill, and manually engineered prompt - on HotpotQA (n=500 per condition) and MATH-500 (n=250). In the primary Qwen v2 rerun under the same frozen protocol, GEPA selects the HotpotQA seed and exactly reproduces baseline behavior, whereas SkillOpt's validation gain reverses into held-out degradation. records.title: Arithmetic and its remedies select the evidence on learned geometry
records.summary: Intelligence that must act before outside correction arrives must carry the structure of its expert knowledge, and hyperbolic geometry represents hierarchy with a fidelity no Euclidean space of comparable dimension matches. Yet hyperbolic language models confine that geometry to adapters or rebuild the transformer, and an independent audit of released hyperbolic vision language checkpoints finds their hierarchy mechanisms inactive, which has been read as evidence about the geometry or its objective. records.title: Accelerated Drift of Scientific Prose in the LLM Era: Evidence from an Interrupted Time-Series Analysis
records.summary: Every scientific text is embedded in the writing norms of its time: it reflects earlier publications while also shaping the texts that follow. The growing use of LLM-based writing tools introduces a new factor in this evolving system, but the linguistic changes coinciding with their emergence remain insufficiently understood. We investigate whether the trajectories of scientific-preprint writing changed in rate or direction after conversational LLMs became publicly accessible, using the release of ChatGPT in November 2022 as the observational breakpoint. records.title: Scaling Synthetic Pre-training Data and Evaluation for Indic LLMs
records.summary: Building capable language models for India requires scalable multilingual data and robust evaluation. We introduce Nemotron-Pretraining-Indic-v1, a synthetic pretraining corpus of approximately 2.83 trillion tokens covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages in native script and twelve in romanized form. It is the largest openly released Indic pretraining corpus. Using our GPU-accelerated pipeline, we translate curated English documents, assess translation quality, and repair low-quality outputs while preserving technical content and document structure and maintaining source traceability. records.title: Do Agents Need a New Kind of Paper? SPRA: Structured Paper Representation for Agents
records.summary: Scientific agents must connect research problems, methods, and findings dispersed through narrative articles. We introduce SPRA (Structured Paper Representation for Agents), a paper-level representation of persistent research objects and typed relations. Its empirical-AI profile organizes Problems, Contributions, Components, ExperimentSetups, Measures, and Findings for querying, traversal, and reuse. Selected paper-level citation relations record dependencies, component use, and comparisons with prior work; source locations support verification. records.title: TempoMoE: Identifying and Steering Fast-Slow Thinking Experts for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
records.summary: Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning models rely on long chain-of-thought (CoT) for complex tasks, yet often overthink easy inputs, increasing token cost and latency, and sometimes degrading accuracy. Existing methods optimize reasoning length during training or impose external control at inference, but leave the underlying reasoning mechanism a black box. We find that fast and slow thinking exhibit distinct expert-routing patterns: holding the input fixed and varying only the prompted reasoning tempo produces stable routing shifts. records.title: Latent Abstraction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
records.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a standard approach for enhancing large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge, mitigating hallucinations, and improving factuality. However, existing systems rely on generating natural language queries at each hop and maintaining a strict architectural separation between retriever and generator, preventing them from leveraging the full representational capacity of the LLM. We propose \textbf{LAnR} (Latent Abstraction for RAG), a unified framework in which a single LLM jointly performs encoding, retrieval, and generation entirely within its own latent space. records.title: Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization
records.summary: Self-distillation policy optimization provides dense token-level supervision for LLM post-training through feedback-conditioned self-teachers. However, directly matching the self-teacher can disrupt successful behaviors on correct rollouts while providing insufficient correction on incorrect ones. We propose Asymmetric Policy Optimization via Self-Distillation (APSD), which constructs correctness-dependent targets by mixing student and self-teacher distributions: interpolation preserves successful behaviors on correct rollouts, while extrapolation beyond the self-teacher strengthens correction on incorrect ones. records.title: GLOBE: Geometry-Led Online Behavioral Early Exit via Unit-Sphere Trajectories
records.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning can improve problem solving, but models often keep generating after the correct answer is already reachable; the extra steps raise serving costs and may replace a correct intermediate result with an incorrect one. We propose GLOBE (Geometry-Led Online Behavioral Early Exit), an online, training-free algorithm that terminates the model's CoT process early. records.title: Bayesian Preference Learning for Test-Time Steerable Reward Models
records.summary: Reward models are central to aligning language models with human preferences via reinforcement learning (RL). As RL is increasingly applied to settings such as verifiable rewards and multi-objective alignment, RMs are expected to encode more complex and multifaceted preference distributions. However, classifier RMs remain static once trained, limiting their adaptability at test time. records.title: Identifying and Mitigating Bottlenecks in Role-Playing Agents: A Systematic Study of Disentangling Character Profile Axes
records.summary: While Large Language Model (LLM) role-playing agents have advanced rapidly, it remains unclear which profile elements genuinely drive role-playing quality. To bridge this gap, we introduce a systematic diagnostic framework that disentangles the impact of character profiles along three axes: Familiarity (Known vs. Unknown), Structure (Structured vs. Unstructured), and Disposition (Moral vs. Immoral). records.title: How to get the best and fairest performance out of your ASR system using activation steering
records.summary: Activation steering for ASR systems is an underexplored technique in improving both ASR performance and demographic fairness. We investigate two forms of activation steering: paired activation subtraction, and supervised optimization. We find the former to be ineffective at ameliorating ASR performance whatsoever, while the latter is quite effective at deriving steering vectors (SVs) that improve at once overall ASR performance and demographic fairness along such diverse axes as gender, age, and dialect. records.title: AdaExploreBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Proactive Exploration and Test-time Adaptation in Evolving Environments
records.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in unfamiliar and evolving environments, requiring them to proactively explore, understand, and adapt to environmental dynamics.
