records.title: Enhancing RAG-based Medical VQA with Gated Multimodal Representations
records.summary: Medical Vision-Language Models (Med-LVLMs) have shown strong performance in Medical Visual Question Answering (MVQA), yet they may still produce factually inconsistent responses. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) can mitigate this issue by incorporating external clinical evidence; however, retrieval is often guided by a single modality, potentially overlooking the joint semantics of medical images and clinical questions. We introduce a multimodal RAG framework that learns a joint query representation through a Gated Multimodal Unit, enabling evidence retrieval to leverage information from both modalities while keeping the underlying Med-LVLM frozen. We evaluate the proposed approach on …

records.title: Analyzing Occupational Gender Bias across the LLM Training Lifecycle
records.summary: Post-training is widely assumed to reduce the social biases language models inherit from pretraining, yet direct evidence for this assumption remains mixed. In this paper, we examine how gender disparities evolve across the language modeling pipeline. In particular, we study occupational gender bias in OLMo 3, a fully open language model family, across its post-training stages by prompting each checkpoint to generate open-ended narratives about synthetic personas given their occupation and education. We consider two settings, a gender-given setting in which the profile states the persona's gender explicitly and a gender-assumed setting in which it must be inferred by the model. We find that …

records.title: MARS: Memory-Aware Routing for Session-Level LLM Assistants
records.summary: Long-term LLM assistants must repeatedly decide what prior context to expose and which model should answer as an interaction evolves. Existing memory systems and model routers usually make these decisions separately, although memory construction changes the evidence, distractors, and difficulty of the resulting input. We introduce MARS, a memory-aware routing framework that uses session state as a shared control interface between memory construction and model selection. A Query and Topic Manager (QTM) estimates compact decision-relevant state that guides a fixed state-conditioned memory policy and an online router, enabling each turn to receive an appropriate memory view and a suitable …

records.title: PragReST: Self-Reinforcing Counterfactual Reasoning for Pragmatic Language Understanding
records.summary: Natural language understanding often depends on meanings that are implied rather than explicitly stated, requiring pragmatic reasoning. Despite strong performance on math and logical reasoning, large language models (LLMs) still struggle with making pragmatic inferences, often choosing literal interpretations. To improve LLM pragmatic reasoning, we introduce PragReST, a self-supervised framework that constructs pragmatic QA data, generates counterfactual reasoning traces, and trains models to internalize them through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, without human-labeled training data or distillation from a stronger teacher. Across four pragmatic benchmarks (PragMega, …

records.title: Towards Reliable Truth-Aligned Uncertainty Estimation in Large Language Models
records.summary: Uncertainty estimation (UE) aims to quantify uncertainty in large language model (LLM) outputs to flag potential hallucinations and support reliable deployment. However, UE metrics often exhibit unstable performance across models and datasets, limiting their practical utility. We formalise this phenomenon as proxy failure, arising because UE metrics are derived from model behaviour rather than being explicitly grounded in factual correctness. We show that when mutual information between a UE score and correctness is low, the score's discriminability must be close to chance. To address this, we propose Truth AnChoring (TAC), a lightweight post-hoc calibration method that maps raw UE scores …

records.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
records.summary: A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting. When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory. We introduce MIST, an evaluation that separates the change from the memory it should leave behind. The model first sets the scene while the change stays hidden, and only later is asked to show it, with leakage before that point kept under control. This separation locates the bottleneck: the model sets the scene but does not …

records.title: ConvexLLM: Scaling Convex-Hull Speech Interfaces to General-Purpose Audio Intelligence
records.summary: Speech and audio language models connect continuous acoustic representations to decoders pretrained primarily on text data. Most such models use MLP or Q-Former interfaces to map acoustic features into the decoder's input space, requiring the decoder to learn how to interpret the resulting representations. We investigate whether grounding these representations in the decoder's existing text embeddings can help it use acoustic information while better preserving its pretrained text capabilities. We present ConvexLLM, a general-purpose speech and audio language model whose C-Gate interface represents audio as continuous convex combinations of frozen text embeddings. ConvexLLM achieves an …

records.title: Referring Multi-Object Tracking with Diverse Dynamic Expressions
records.summary: Referring understanding is a fundamental task that bridges natural language and visual content by localizing objects described in free-form expressions. However, existing works are constrained by limited language expressiveness, lacking the capacity to model object dynamics in spatial numbers and temporal states. To address these limitations, we introduce a new and general referring understanding task, termed referring multi-object tracking (RMOT). Its core idea is to employ a language expression as a semantic cue to guide the prediction of multi-object tracking, comprehensively accounting for variations in object quantity and temporal semantics. Along with RMOT, we introduce a RMOT …

records.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
records.summary: Speculative decoding speeds up large language model inference: a small drafter proposes several tokens, and the target model verifies them in one parallel pass. Drafting a tree lets the target verify many alternative continuations at once. DDTree builds such trees from the block-diffusion drafter DFlash, but scores each position independently of the tokens earlier in its branch; Domino conditions on those tokens but drafts only a single chain. DominoTree combines the two: a training-free best-first tree scored by Domino's path-dependent causal correction, restricted to top-M candidates. In a research harness at temperature zero, it averages 5.33x speedup over autoregressive (AR) decoding on …

records.title: EduWild: How Teacher-Configured Chatbots Fail in Real-World Use and How to Fix Them
records.summary: Teachers increasingly configure educational chatbots through natural-language instructions, but how these bots fail in real-world use remains poorly understood. We introduce EduWild, a dataset of 1,726 conversations with 217 teacher-configured chatbots, each paired with the instructions and configuration behind it, including 900 conversations from the intended end users of 35 deployed chatbots. We develop a 29-code taxonomy covering factual, workflow, diagnostic, and pedagogical failures and apply it using a human-calibrated LLM judge. The most frequent failures are lapses in following teacher intent --- bots skip required workflow steps (53.8% of end-user conversations), omit expectation …

records.title: Truth in Contrast: Calibrated Factual Evidence from Language Model Likelihoods
records.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) encode substantial factual knowledge. Yet, estimating confidence in factual claims reliably remains challenging. We study likelihood-based factual confidence from the complementary perspectives of discrimination and calibration across multilingual factual statements. Specifically, we instantiate contrastive generative likelihoods as Contrastive Factual Evidence (CFE), which compares the likelihood of the same claim under competing factual and non-factual conditions, and derive its probabilistic counterpart, the Contrastive Factual Posterior (CFP). We show analytically that CFP calibration depends on the differential error between the two surrogate conditionals, …

records.title: Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can now perceive, describe, and reason about images and audio, yet time series understanding remains underestimated: most work uses LLMs as forecasters and classifiers, reasoning studies are few and narrow, and no suite trains and evaluates the full range of capabilities. In this paper, we build the first such suite, with 337K training and 44K evaluation samples across three progressive capabilities, Perceive, Solve, and Reason, and use it to ask how time series should enter an LLM that must master all three, and in what order. We find that a dedicated encoder is essential: with one, a 4B model surpasses GPT-4o on every perception attribute we test, whereas …

records.title: MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups
records.summary: Research groups that want a language model grounded in their own literature face a choice between hosted services that receive their unpublished work and self-hosted deployments that keep the data local but give the model no access to the corpus. Munin is an open-source framework for a self-hosted scientific assistant that indexes a group's corpus and its citation graph, and wraps whichever open-weight model the group can serve in an agent harness with specialised reading, search, and computation tools. We claim that the harness, rather than the specific model, is what makes the system useful on domain literature, and we ship the evaluation suite that tests this claim with the software. On …

records.title: Test-Time Scaling with Diffusion Language Models via Reward-Guided Stitching
records.summary: Reasoning with large language models often benefits from generating multiple chains-of-thought, but existing aggregation strategies are typically trajectory-level (e.g., selecting the best trace or voting on the final answer), discarding useful intermediate work from partial or "nearly correct" attempts. We propose Stitching Noisy Diffusion Thoughts, a self-consistency framework that turns cheap diffusion-sampled reasoning into a reusable pool of step-level candidates. Given a problem, we (i) sample many diverse, low-cost reasoning trajectories using a masked diffusion language model, (ii) score every intermediate step with an off-the-shelf process reward model (PRM), and (iii) stitch these …

records.title: A low-dimensional dynamical basis for tongue shape control
records.summary: Speech production involves the control of a high-dimensional articulatory system with many degrees-of-freedom, but a widespread hypothesis is that speakers navigate this complexity using a set of lower-dimensional control variables. Common candidates for these control variables include individual articulators (e.g. tongue body) and abstract tract variables (e.g. tongue body constriction location), but identifying the most appropriate coordinate system for articulatory control remains an open question. In this study, we advance a model in which holistic tongue shape modes represent a potential low-dimensional control basis for a simple dynamical law. We first discover empirical tongue shape …

records.title: HydraLLM: Adaptive Width Slicing for Elastic Text and Vision-Language Models
records.summary: LLMs and LVLMs are increasingly deployed across heterogeneous hardware, ranging from data-center GPUs to resource-constrained edge devices. Their fixed-size architectures limit the ability to reuse a single model across deployment settings with different compute, latency, and model-size targets. We introduce HydraLLM, an elastic MQA-based architecture. Its number of active attention heads determines the effective widths of the embeddings, attention projections, feed-forward layers, and the output head, forming a nested family of subnetworks within a single parameter set. We introduce a static-to-elastic conversion pipeline that, starting from a pre-trained model checkpoint, includes …

records.title: "You" Is Not Toxic: How LLM Labelers Rewrite the Web's Conversation Laws
records.summary: What the Web community believes about toxic conversations, such as that toxicity rises in longer and deeper threads, was measured mostly with Google's Perspective API, which is shutting down; large language models (LLMs) will make the next measurements. We find that LLM labelers mistake second-person address for toxicity, and that this one bias manufactures laws that human labels do not show. On 1.25 million news comments with crowd labels, Claude Haiku flags 12% of the non-toxic comments that contain no "you" and 51% of those with four or more; a single crowd rater flags 6% and 10%. Deeper replies address someone more often, so under Haiku toxicity rises with reply depth (+0.93 percentage …

records.title: Atomic Consistency Preference Optimization for Long-Form Question Answering
records.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) often produce factoid hallucinations - plausible yet incorrect answers. A common mitigation strategy is model alignment, which improves factual accuracy by training on curated (factual, non-factual) pairs. However, this approach often relies on a stronger model (e.g., GPT-4) or an external knowledge base to assess factual correctness that may not always be accessible. Addressing this, we propose Atomic Consistency Preference Optimization (ACPO), a self-supervised preference-tuning method that enhances factual accuracy without external supervision. ACPO leverages atomic consistency signals (i.e., the agreement of individual facts across multiple stochastic …

records.title: ScoutRoute: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Routing Using Internal Language Model Signals
records.summary: Efficient expert routing is a fundamental challenge in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) systems, particularly for heterogeneous collections of independently trained Large Language Mod els (LLMs). Existing routing approaches typically rely on jointly trained gating networks, prompt-based predictors, or computationally expensive multi-model inference, limiting their flexibility and efficiency. This paper presents ScoutRoute, a lightweight post-hoc routing framework that predicts expert competence using internal language model signals extracted from a single forward pass through an inexpensive scout model. Hidden-state representations are used to estimate cross-model competence through lightweight …

records.title: Cross-Layer Attention Probing for Fine-Grained Hallucination Detection
records.summary: With the large-scale adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) in various applications, there is a growing reliability concern due to their tendency to generate inaccurate text, i.e. hallucinations. In this work, we propose Cross-Layer Attention Probing (CLAP), a novel activation probing technique for hallucination detection, which processes the LLM activations across the entire residual stream as a joint sequence. Our empirical evaluations using five LLMs and three tasks show that CLAP improves hallucination detection compared to baselines on both greedy decoded responses as well as responses sampled at higher temperatures, thus enabling fine-grained detection, i.e. the ability to …

records.title: On the Tip of the Tongue: First-Token Cueing as a Behavioral Probe of Recall Failures in LLMs
records.summary: Large language models often answer factual questions incorrectly in closed-book settings, and such errors are usually attributed to missing knowledge. Yet models often encode answers they fail to produce. We show that many closed-book errors are first-token recall failures: the model commits to a wrong first token, but once given the right one it completes the answer and often recognizes it as correct. We study this with First-Token Cueing, a behavioral probe that prefills the response with the first token of the gold answer. Model uncertainty peaks at the first answer token, where it already predicts correctness, and among gold prefixes of any length the first token alone accounts for the …

records.title: Sentence-Level Topic Modeling with Lexical and Contextual Evidence
records.summary: Topic modeling faces a fundamental granularity dilemma: probabilistic topic models assign topics at the word level, whereas transformer-based methods operate at the document level. The latter overlooks that real-world documents typically cover multiple topics, whereas the former relies on individual words, which rarely provide sufficient context to identify them. We introduce SentenceETM, a neural topic model that assigns a topic to each sentence by jointly using lexical and contextual evidence. Each topic is described both by a distribution over the vocabulary, defined through word embeddings, and by a Gaussian over sentence embeddings concentrated on a topic-specific low-dimensional …

records.title: FSPO: Policy-Consistent Risk and Pareto-Feasible Control for Budgeted LLM RL Post-Training
records.summary: Adaptive LLM reinforcement-learning post-training changes multiple training actuators online, including rollout temperature, group size, clipping, KL regularization, verifier allocation, and update budget. Three coupled issues remain unresolved. A future-risk model trained from behavior trajectories need not estimate the risk induced by the controller that will be deployed; a score calibrated on logged state-action pairs can become miscalibrated after selective action choice; and independent per-resource minimum costs do not in general certify a feasible multi-resource continuation. We introduce FSPO, a feedback-state controller for budgeted LLM RL post-training that addresses these issues …

records.title: Two Minds Better Than One: Collaborative Reward Modeling for LLM Alignment
records.summary: Reward models (RMs) are central to aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values, yet noisy preference feedback can induce reward misgeneralization through spurious correlations and overfitting. We characterize the training dynamics of preference pairs and uncover a distinctive optimization signature of noise: persistently high losses, sharp temporal fluctuations, and irregular gradient updates. Our analyses further show that excluding such pairs improves downstream alignment. In practice, however, reliable preferences are not known a priori, and self-filtering based on a model's own training signals can amplify confirmation bias. To address this challenge, we introduce …

records.title: Actions with Receipts: Jointly Binding Claims, Evidence, and Execution for Replayable Tool-Agent Auditing
records.summary: Tool-using agents can expose citations and execution logs while leaving a critical association unaudited: whether the claim shown to a user is the claim emitted by the committed execution and supported by the cited source. A valid citation and a valid trace can therefore remain individually well formed while being transplanted across claims, actions, runs, or source versions. We introduce a claim-anchored execution contract that jointly binds the emitted claim, its exact source span, the ordered execution prefix that produced it, and the source version and access state observed by that execution. records.title: ROUTEAUDIT: Interaction-Aware Identification for Budgeted Multi-Verifier Routing
records.summary: Adaptive multi-verifier systems are commonly compared through endpoint quality-cost gaps, even when the verifier catalog, availability, accounting, information filtration, or scorer changes with the policy. We formulate verifier routing as a contract-conditioned identification problem. The contract records request support, verifier catalog, realized availability, resource accounting, online filtration, and post-trace scoring; a matched route contrast changes only the policy coordinate. ROUTEAUDIT adds three measurable objects to this contract. records.title: ContractRL: Shielded Group-Relative Policy Optimization for Auditable Tool-Call Repair
records.summary: Structured tool calls often fail after only a small number of fields violate a schema or an execution contract. Regenerating the complete object enlarges the action surface and makes repeated repair difficult to audit. We introduce ContractRL, a contract-constrained sequential repair protocol that models verifier-guided JSON repair as a bounded decision process. At each step the policy observes the candidate, typed verifier feedback, JSON Pointer, immutable repair history, and remaining budget; a contract-derived action mask filters malformed or prohibited RFC-6902 operations before a deterministic validator performs the transition. records.title: Dependency Reasoning for Aspect Sentiment Quadruple Prediction
records.summary: Aspect Sentiment Quadruple Prediction (ASQP) is fundamentally a relational reasoning problem: identifying aspect-opinion-category-sentiment quadruples requires modeling structured dependencies, not merely sequential co-occurrence. Existing LLM-based approaches incorporate syntactic information indirectly, via retrieval-based demonstration selection or multi-stage training, rather than as unified, single-pass generation-time context. We present DRIFT, which linearizes dependency parse trees and injects them directly into LLM prompts as explicit relational context, enabling the model to reason over aspect-opinion dependencies rather than infer them from token proximity alone. DRIFT further …

records.title: VStress: Correlation-Aware Auditing and Adaptive Budget Allocation for Repeated Verifiers
records.summary: Repeated verifier calls are useful only when they contribute conditional information. We introduce VStress, an auditable replay contract, and VStress-CA, a correlation-aware allocation policy that estimates the conditional marginal information of an unqueried verifier on a sealed calibration split, discounts uncertainty, normalizes by call cost, and stops or abstains when the next call is not informative. The controller freezes its decision and cost ledger before joining the clean oracle; a dependence-shift alarm disables channel preference and falls back to exact-stop. The controlled audit gives the mechanism boundary: at 35% symmetric corruption, majority-5 improves balanced accuracy from …

records.title: FAER: Auditable Utility-Aligned Trajectory Replay for Language Model Post-Training
records.summary: Replay selectors often rank cached trajectories by format feedback, confidence, freshness, or response length, although cache-level correctness and downstream learner utility are distinct objectives. We formalize this selection-to-learning gap and introduce FAER as an auditable full-trajectory replay framework. Its training-free fixed selector is a protocol baseline; FAER-UTILITY is the learner-aware selector fitted on disjoint calibration blocks. The normalized gradient alignment is reported as a baseline, while a disposable optimizer-aware virtual update supplies a magnitude-aware utility surface. The audit contract freezes observed fields and replay traces before evaluation labels are …

records.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning (RL) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model-training run. Even at ten GPU-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable as …

records.title: CDAE: Enhancing Perturbation Robustness in Pretrained Language Models with Contrastive Denoising
records.summary: Pre-trained language models have significantly improved sentence representation learning, yet their embeddings remain sensitive to textual perturbations such as synonym substitution, masking, and word dropout. This work proposes a lightweight Contrastive Denoising Autoencoder (CDAE) that refines pre-trained BERT embeddings by jointly optimizing contrastive and reconstruction objectives to learn perturbation-invariant representations. We evaluate the proposed framework under multiple perturbation strategies and strengths, and compare it against the original BERT embeddings and SimCSE. Experimental results show that CDAE consistently preserves higher embedding similarity under perturbation, …

records.title: Robust Function Calling for LLM Agents Under Interface Drift
records.summary: Tool-augmented language-model agents rely on interface text: tool descriptions, argument schemas, and the candidate tool list shown at inference time. These interfaces often change after deployment even when the underlying tool semantics remain fixed, creating a practical reliability problem for function-calling systems. We study this failure mode as interface drift and evaluate whether a lightweight, training-free repair layer can recover robustness without retraining the base model. Our method, SchemaShield-Lite, combines schema validation, candidate-set retry for missing tool names, and one-shot constrained repair. On Qwen3.5-9B, it raises DICE-300 accuracy from 0.717 to 0.813 and …

records.title: Audit-First VAPO: Risk-Certified Selective Updates under Imperfect Verification
records.summary: Imperfect verifiers can assign a harmful update direction even when clipping and regularization bound its magnitude. We introduce Audit-First VAPO, which separates discrete directional admission from continuous magnitude control. An observation-only accept-appeal-abstain policy uses a finite secondary-verification budget; its action trace is frozen before clean labels are joined. Simultaneous finite-sample bounds then certify selected harmful risk, coverage, and verifier-call rate over a predeclared policy family. Conditional Hoeffding-Azuma bounds account for the dependence induced by shared budgets, and rollout or verifier changes initiate a new certification stage. After admission, a …

records.title: RubricEM: Meta-RL with Rubric-guided Policy Decomposition beyond Verifiable Rewards
records.summary: Deep research agents plan, search, evaluate evidence, and synthesize long-form reports. Training these agents with reinforcement learning (RL) is challenging because they operate over long horizons and their outputs lack exact answer verifiers. To this end, we introduce RubricEM, a unified RL framework for deep research that combines stagewise credit assignment with reflection-based meta-RL for experience reuse. Rubrics unify the framework by providing a shared interface for policy execution, judge feedback, and experience reuse. RubricEM first instills a rubric-guided scaffold through supervised fine-tuning, teaching the agent to plan with rubrics and organize its trajectory into semantic …

records.title: HyperPersona: A Multi-Level Hypergraph Framework for Text-Based Automatic Personality Prediction
records.summary: As a modern commodity, language has become a vast repository of socially and psychologically significant traits and concepts, reflecting the ways people encode pattern of thoughts, behaviors, and emotions into words. Text-based Automatic Personality Prediction (APP), seeks to infer personality from linguistic behavior, offering a scalable alternative to traditional psychometric assessments. records.title: CascadeLedger: Counterfactual Auditing of Information and Resource Integrity in LLM Cascades
records.summary: We introduce CascadeLedger, a counterfactual execution-audit framework for budgeted language-model cascades. The protocol enforces call-before-read semantics, binds successful reads to service and cache identities, records availability and component-wise budget transitions, and freezes the event trace before any target or task scorer is joined. The central object is aggregate-equivalent trace validity: two executions can share a final answer, declared resource projection, and service histogram while differing in whether their routing decisions used only legitimately observable information. records.title: Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT): Evidence-Based Text Generation via a Closed-Loop Retrieve--Reflect--Revise Pipeline on Edge LLMs
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent outputs that lack source support or conflict with local operational constraints. We introduce Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT), a modular architecture that organizes generation as a closed Retrieve--Reflect--Revise loop. SRCoT separates environment state, persistent knowledge, accumulated experience, and short-term memory into provenance-labeled stores. BM25 retrieval supplies local context; subsequent passes expose intermediate drafts, missing-information markers, follow-up queries, and optional claim--evidence mappings. records.title: Inferring L1 Backgrounds from L2 English with LLM Token Probabilities
records.summary: Native language identification (NLI) infers a non-native speaker's first language (L1) from their second language (L2) production. We investigate a token probability approach that scores each text sample as a continuation of a prompt prefix specifying a candidate L1, then predicts the candidate with the highest score. We evaluate our approach using Llama 3.1 8B and 70B on three datasets: TOEFL9, Write and Improve 2024, and BULATS-L1. We compare its performance with previous prompting-based classification approaches. records.title: SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation
records.summary: A key challenge in on-policy distillation (OPD) is extracting effective supervision from teacher knowledge. Supervision from token probabilities may underutilize internal knowledge, while direct hidden-state matching forces the student to shift to the teacher's feature space and complicates cross-architecture transfer. Inspired by contrastive learning's use of relationships between instances, we propose \textbf{SimOPD} to transfer teacher internal knowledge through response similarities. Specifically, SimOPD uses paired memory banks of student-generated responses to extract supervision from the teacher's internal representations as similarity distributions. records.title: Verbalising Model's Computation for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Detection
records.summary: Current Chain-of-Thought (CoT) verification methods detect reasoning faithfulness from model outputs or static activations, but are limited in explaining how unfaithfulness develops during generation. We introduce VERITAS to verbalise the model's computation: how different reasoning anchors emerge, transfer across layers, and surface in the output. VERITAS adopts the layer-wise Jacobian projection to produce a verbalised account of the model's internal reasoning evolution at each generated CoT token. records.title: SpaceCast-Bench: Evaluating Predictive Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
records.summary: Existing spatial reasoning benchmarks mainly test spatial perception: reading off relations already visible in the input. Yet real-world spatial intelligence demands predictive spatial reasoning: constructing a scene from observations, anticipating how an intervention changes it, and reasoning about the unseen outcome. We introduce SpaceCast-Bench, the first benchmark to directly and diagnostically evaluate this capability. Built around an observe-transform-infer framework, its 3,862 questions from 182 real-world scenes span 16 task types at three levels: static perception, local prediction, and global prediction, progressively requiring scene understanding, spatial state updating, and …

records.title: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To
records.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) controllability, the ability of reasoning models to control properties of their CoT, is consequential for both their usefulness and reliable oversight. Recent work evaluates this capability by measuring whether models follow CoT constraints given in the user prompt, and reports very low controllability across models. We argue that this low controllability may not reflect an inherent inability of reasoning models to control their CoT, but instead result from naively specifying constraints in the user prompt. To test this, we introduce Self-Instructed CoT Controllability: a complementary evaluation that places the constraint as a self-instruction inside the model's CoT …

records.title: Sample, Mix, or Verify? Allocating Test-Time Compute under Imperfect Verifiers
records.summary: A common way to make language models and agents more accurate is to spend more compute at inference time: generate many candidate solutions and submit the one a verifier prefers. Success then requires that some candidate is correct and that the verifier picks it. The first grows predictably with the number of samples; the second does not, because real verifiers (unit tests, majority votes, LLM judges, reward models) accept wrong answers, reject right ones, and make correlated mistakes. With a fixed budget, a practitioner must decide how many samples to draw, which models to draw them from, and how much to spend on verification, and today these choices are made by rules of thumb. records.title: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents
records.summary: Tool-using agents read untrusted external content, which exposes them to indirect prompt injection (IPI), where hidden instructions hijack the agent's tool calls. Benchmarks measure IPI security by the attack success rate (ASR), which treats every failed attack as a successful defense. To test this assumption, we audit 33,000 trajectories from eleven open-weight agents (2-14B parameters) on InjecAgent and AgentDojo. A label-blind LLM judge shows that most failed attacks are ignored (76-80%) rather than refused (17-18%). records.title: LLM Evolution in a Simple Simulated Market
records.summary: Arguments that AI systems will evolve in harmful ways are largely made in the abstract. We provide a concrete empirical example. We simulate simple markets consisting of populations of twenty Large Language Model agents tasked with solving arithmetic problems. Agents differ only in their system prompt; those that go bankrupt are removed and replaced by mutated copies of the prompts of successful agents. Two market conditions select for opposite phenotypes: a market that rewards accuracy produces agents with high accuracy (94%) and high token use; a market that charges per token produces agents with low accuracy (10%) and low token use. In the second market, only tokens are incentivised yet …

records.title: Who Pays for Efficient Inference? Confidence-Based Small-to-Large LLM Routing Across Tasks and Languages
records.summary: Small-to-large language model routing can reduce inference cost by escalating difficult inputs while retaining easier ones on a smaller model. Its success, however, depends on identifying examples that benefit from escalation, and the reliability of confidence across multilingual tasks remains unclear. We present a systematic evaluation of confidence-based routing across three model families, four languages, and three task types, covering 72 model, dataset, language, and scale configurations and 42,288 predictions. We compare global confidence routing with random routing, equal-quota confidence routing, and an oracle upper bound. Confidence identifies beneficial escalations on the Belebele …

records.title: Think More or Read More? A Token-Budget Theory of Reasoning with Shared Context
records.summary: Reasoning systems increasingly improve answers by incorporating additional context into the model's input, from multi-agent debate, where agents read their peers' responses, to self-refinement, where a model revisits its own drafts. In these systems, communication consumes context as one agent's output becomes another's input. records.title: AgentOdyssey: Open-Ended Long-Horizon Text Game Generation for Test-Time Continual Learning Agents
records.summary: For agents to learn continuously from interaction with the world at test time, they must be able to explore effectively, acquire new world knowledge and skills, retain relevant episodic experiences, and plan over long horizons. To evaluate these key abilities of test-time continual learning agents, we introduce AgentOdyssey, a novel evaluation framework that procedurally generates open-ended text games with rich entities, world dynamics, and long-horizon tasks. records.title: Bengali Hallucination Detection with Retrieval and Programs: A System Study
records.summary: Bengali hallucination detection must distinguish unsupported factual claims from incorrect reasoning, often without a supplied reference passage. We present and characterize an inference-only system that combines response-conditioned query rewriting, hybrid retrieval, and task-specific language-model judging. Six retrieval routes search question-answer and passage collections; a router directs each example to a 27B textual judge or a 14B agent that can compare retrieved answers, reason directly, or generate and execute Python. We characterize the system using version-specific code, saved predictions, execution traces, and corpus metadata from the Olikbochon challenge. Kaggle associates a …

records.title: NLData2Opt: Benchmarking Parameter Derivation and Prediction for Modeling Optimization Problems from Natural Language and Data
records.summary: Formulating optimization problems from raw inputs of problem descriptions and data is time-consuming and costly. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising way to automate this process, existing benchmarks overestimate their capabilities by relying on idealized inputs where all data is relevant and complete. This diverges from reality, where data-centric reasoning is required to extract, compute, and predict parameters from noisy sources. To address this, we introduce NLData2Opt, a benchmark to evaluate LLMs on the multi-stage reasoning inherent in practical optimization workflows. NLData2Opt decomposes problems into problem descriptions and data, and requires models to (1) …

records.title: Cooperation Without Adaptation: LLM Agents in a Collective-Risk Dilemma
records.summary: Language-model agents are increasingly deployed to act on behalf of people in settings where individual decisions shape shared outcomes. We examine whether five production models adapt their contributions to changing risks and partner behaviour, or instead follow a relatively fixed strategy. In a collective-risk dilemma game (CRG), six players contribute to a shared pool over ten rounds; if the pool falls short of its target, a catastrophe may destroy their remaining resources. Four models contributed approximately an equal share at every positive risk level, and four of the five also contributed when risk was zero, even though contributing could not improve their payoff. records.title: TimpaTeks: Automatic In-place Text Sequence Modification via Diffusion Language Model Steering
records.summary: We extend activation steering to diffusion language models (DLMs) and study a novel problem that arose due to the inference mechanism of DLMs: Modifying a text in-place to manifest a different concept. We propose TimpaTeks, an automatic in-place text modification mechanism using DLMs. Experiments on IMDB movie reviews (sentiment) and a synthetic Cats and Dogs Dataset (arbitrary, more unconventional concept steering) show that TimpaTeks provides a feasible novel mechanism to steer diffusion language model outputs in-place. records.title: Safety Alignment via Constrained Knowledge Unlearning
records.summary: Despite significant progress in safety alignment, large language models (LLMs) remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks. Existing defense mechanisms have not fully deleted harmful knowledge in LLMs, which allows such attacks to bypass safeguards and produce harmful outputs. To address this challenge, we propose a novel safety alignment strategy, Constrained Knowledge Unlearning (CKU), which focuses on two primary objectives: knowledge localization and retention, and unlearning harmful knowledge. CKU works by scoring neurons in specific multilayer perceptron (MLP) layers to identify a subset U of neurons associated with useful knowledge. records.title: Identify, Classify, Act: Per-Instruction Controlled Compliance for LLMs over External Data
records.summary: LLMs over external data face a per-instruction tension: a single document or tool return often interleaves legitimate directives with adversarial prompt injections, and the model must follow the former while rejecting the latter. Existing defenses suppress or trust all external instructions, collapsing the safety-utility frontier and forcing a choice between over-refusal and over-compliance. We argue the missing capability is \textbf{per-instruction credit attribution} and formalize it as External-Data Instruction Classification, an identify-classify-act decision over each embedded directive. records.title: Is MT Ready for the Next Crisis or Pandemic?
records.summary: Communication in times of crisis is essential. However, there is often a mismatch between the language of governments, aid providers, doctors, and those to whom they are providing aid. It is reasonable to turn to commercial MT tools in these scenarios. But how effective are these tools for translating to and from low resource languages, particularly in the crisis or medical domain? In this study, we evaluate 5 commercial systems used for MT (Google Translate, Microsoft Translator, GPT, Gemini and Claude) against the TICO-19 dataset, which contains pandemic-related sentences from a large set of high-priority languages spoken by communities most likely to be adversely affected in the next …

records.title: Language Model Goal Selection Differs from Humans' in a Self-Directed Learning Task
records.summary: Whether in agentic workflows, social studies, or chat settings, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being asked to replace humans in choosing which goals to pursue, rather than completing predefined tasks. However, the assumption that LLMs accurately reflect human preferences for goal setting remains largely untested. We assess the validity of LLMs as proxies for human goal selection in a controlled, self-directed learning task borrowed from cognitive science. Across five models (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Qwen3 32B, and Centaur), we find substantial divergence from human behavior. records.title: LoongSage: A Production-Grade, High-Efficiency Agentic RL Framework for Frontier LLMs with Validated Recipes
records.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a critical phase in the post-training pipeline of large language models (LLMs). As the frontier of LLM capabilities shifts from static reasoning to agentic tasks--characterized by external tool invocation, multi-turn interactions, and long-horizon decision-making--existing mainstream RL frameworks have grown increasingly unwieldy, raising the overhead of adoption, usage, and debugging. To address these challenges, we present LoongSage, an agent-native, fully asynchronous RL framework with a lightweight core of roughly 14K lines of code. records.title: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search
records.summary: Tree search enhances multi-step reasoning in large language models (LLMs), yet prevailing methods expand every step with a fixed budget, irrespective of the marginal utility of expansion. records.title: The Reliance Hypothesis: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Rises as Language Resource Level Falls
records.summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) faithfulness matters for monitoring, explaining and safely deploying large language models, yet it has been studied mostly in English. Languages differ in level, the amount of text available to learn from, so models know less in lower-resource languages, which may change how much they rely on their reasoning. To our knowledge, we are the first to relate CoT faithfulness to both resource level and task type (knowledge- or reasoning-intensive). records.title: Too Emotional to Be Fake? Intra-Utterance Emotion Shifts Expose Failure Modes in Speech Deepfake Detectors
records.summary: Expressive speech synthesis can now change emotion within a single utterance, yet its impact on deepfake detection remains unclear. We introduce EmoShift, a benchmark comparing emotion-stable (AA) and emotion-changing (AB) speech to examine these effects while accounting for static emotion identity and acoustic confounds. It comprises 7,240 bona fide utterances from four source datasets and 9,720 synthetic utterances generated using four expressive TTS systems. Across seven detectors, we find that emotion changes can make synthetic speech appear more genuine, increasing spoof miss rates by up to 25.3 percentage points on OMG-Emotion at fixed thresholds. records.title: Causal Edit Serialization
records.summary: Standard autoregressive language models generate text sequentially, but revision requires referring back to tokens in the input context or those already generated. Causal Edit Serialization (CES) is introduced as a framework for expressing such revisions within the same causal token stream. Special pointer tokens are paired with predicted source addresses, allowing insertion, deletion, replacement, copying and movement to be localized explicitly. records.summary: Language-model watermarks can help identify model-generated text, encode provenance information, and detect post-generation edits. records.title: On the Position Bias of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Study
records.summary: Recent studies have shown that position bias remains a critical vulnerability in large language models (LLMs), undermining both the integrity of multiple-choice evaluations and the reliability of retrieval-augmented generation. However, existing understanding of this phenomenon is largely derived from studies with limited model coverage and English-centric benchmarks, leaving the behavior of frontier models and diverse languages underexplored. In this work, we conduct a comprehensive investigation of position bias across model scales ranging from billion-level to trillion-level parameters, covering both multiple-choice and multi-document tasks in five languages. records.title: Veil-Then-Reveal: Protecting PII Privacy via Reversible Pseudo-Anonymization in Zero-Trust User--LLM Interaction
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly process sensitive documents and personal information, yet sending prompts containing personally identifiable information (PII) to remote providers exposes data subjects and organizations to risks from logging, retention, model training, and unintended disclosure. Existing anonymization methods often mask or remove PII, while conventional encryption eliminates the lexical and structural cues needed for effective LLM processing. records.summary: Reasoning rerankers write a rationale before ranking a candidate slate, and existing systems read item metadata to do so, even though generative recommenders increasingly represent items as compact Semantic IDs (SIDs). records.summary: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on proprietary records enables domain adaptation but introduces two challenges: (i) privacy leakage of memorized private data, such as personally identifiable information (PII), and (ii) balancing private data removal with utility preservation. records.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
records.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment. records.summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have given rise to time-series question answering (TSQA), which formulates time-series analysis as natural-language question answering. records.summary: Every multilingual speech pipeline begins with a language decision, an error there propagates silently through recognition, translation and routing. In India it spans 22 scheduled languages across four language families, heard over short, noisy, narrowband and code-mixed audio. records.summary: Language models that read financial news are usually trained on text from the same years used to test them, so a backtest can reward hindsight. We build news topics from NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, adapted into a sentence encoder by contrastive fine-tuning on passages of the same article, with no labels or returns. records.title: Thunder-DeID+: Boundary-Aware Korean De-identification from Court Judgments to Broader Sensitive Documents

The agglutinative structure of Korean causes Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizers to frequently merge Personally Identifiable Information (PII) with adjacent particles, which complicates accurate span recovery. records.title: TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
records.summary: Advances in frontier coding agents have sharply increased the token costs of AI-assisted software engineering. Their token efficiency is typically evaluated on isolated tasks, whereas real-world developers use them to continuously build, update, and maintain large-scale projects. This mismatch motivates us to evaluate agents over sequences of realistic coding tasks, where we find that agents exhibit recurring environment-dependent token costs that existing methods struggle to reduce. records.title: A misinformation playbook sharpens judgement without breeding cynicism
records.summary: Misinformation harms public health and democracy, and generative artificial intelligence now writes falsehoods as persuasive as people's. Defences range from fact-checking individual claims to training people to resist falsehoods. Yet many claims are too new to check, and interventions that teach doubt can reduce belief in truth too. records.summary: Large language model (LLM) unlearning aims to forget certain information while preserving others, without retraining from scratch. records.summary: Language models can be sampled multiple times to access the distribution underlying their responses, but existing methods cannot efficiently synthesize rich epistemic signals across different long-form responses. records.summary: Large reasoning models solve complex problems through long chains of thought, in which prior work has documented failure modes such as overthinking, underthinking, and unsupported deductions. records.title: EdgeWise: Bringing Long-Horizon Agents to the Edge via Selective Cloud Delegation
records.summary: Complex and long-horizon agent tasks often rely on frontier models deployed in the cloud to achieve strong performance. records.summary: Refusal is a common safety mechanism in large language models (LLMs), yet in contexts of suicidal ideation (SI), refusing to engage can itself constitute a safety failure. records.title: GlobeBench: Evaluating Text-Based World Model Capabilities for Scalable Environment Simulations
records.summary: Text-based world models have recently shown potential to simulate complex RL environment state transitions for a diverse set of use cases. records.summary: Large language model agents must discover relevant tools from large libraries, e.g., thousands of tools, as new needs arise during task execution. records.title: Multimodal Filesystem Memory For Long-Horizon Embodied Agents
records.summary: Agents operating over long horizons need an effective memory that allows them to reuse their experience throughout long interactions. records.title: Not All Graphs Are Maps: A Task-Agnostic Exploration Framework for Mobile GUI Navigation
records.summary: Modern mobile GUI agents can perceive visible screens and execute local actions, but they still lack persistent app-specific navigation knowledge: where functions live, which pages contain them, and which screens are equivalent across repeated visits. records.summary: A fundamental challenge in evaluating and training autonomous agents is measuring the intrinsic difficulty of the tasks they attempt. records.summary: Online communities provide spaces for individuals navigating stressful life transitions to disclose difficulties and seek peer support. We introduce SpecAgent, a collaboration protocol that turns the strong model from the author of each step into a reviewer of steps drafted by a weak model. records.title: Translation Circuit Discovery and Targeted Optimization for Low-Resource Multilingual Translation
records.summary: Recent multilingual large language models achieve strong translation performance, yet the internal mechanisms responsible for low-resource multilingual translation remain insufficiently understood. In this paper, we study translation circuits in multilingual decoder-only LLMs for Hindi-to-Urdu and Hindi-to-Sindhi (Devanagari). We propose TITAN, a mechanistic framework that combines causal intervention, sparse feature decomposition, and targeted preference optimization to identify and optimize crucial translation components in the transformer. Unlike conventional full-parameter fine-tuning, TITAN restricts optimization to sparse, causally important circuits, enabling scalable and …

records.title: C-VARC: A Large-Scale Chinese Value Rule Corpus for Value Alignment of Large Language Models
records.summary: Aligning LLMs with Chinese values requires culturally grounded resources that connect abstract values to concrete behavioral guidance. We introduce C-VARC, a Chinese Value Rule Corpus containing 257,609 Rules of Thumb (RoTs) organized into three dimensions, 12 core values, and 50 derived values. Among them, 36,000 rules underwent independent human review by two annotators (Cohen's kappa>0.85), with disagreements adjudicated by a third. C-VARC supports reusable rule-driven pipelines for both value evaluation and model alignment. records.title: SITAR: A Situational Distortion Metric for Automatic Speech Recognition Evaluation
records.summary: In automatic speech recognition (ASR), transcription errors with similar lexical or semantic discrepancies can have markedly different consequences for the situation conveyed by speech. Capturing these differences requires not merely contextual assessment, but an understanding of what the spoken discourse describes, establishes, or seeks to bring about. However, relying on LLM judges introduces computational cost and scoring variability. We introduce SITAR, a situational distortion metric for ASR, realized through a comprehensive end-to-end construction framework. Specifically, this framework aggregates situational severity and cumulative extent into a unified score via a bounded recursive …

records.title: M$^3$R-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Metaphor Understanding
records.summary: Multimodal metaphor understanding requires identifying cross-domain Target-Source mappings and inferring sentiment from visual and textual evidence. However, existing benchmarks largely evaluate these subtasks separately and lack evidence-grounded explanations, limiting their ability to assess coherent cross-modal reasoning. To enable unified and evidence-grounded evaluation, we introduce M$^3$R-Bench, a benchmark of 1,000 human-annotated image-text instances with joint labels for metaphor occurrence, Target-Source mapping, and sentiment, alongside stage-wise explanations for evidence identification, mapping establishment, and sentiment inference. records.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
records.summary: Modern agent frameworks equip large language models with external skill libraries to solve complex tasks. However, it remains unclear whether these systems can effectively evolve their skills and whether the resulting skills improve task-solving capabilities. To bridge this gap, we introduce ContinualSkillBench, a dynamic evaluation framework for in-context continual skill learning. It covers five domains, each with 100 tasks ordered by difficulty and opportunities for skill transfer. Our experiments show that sequential execution generally improves performance, but the gains vary substantially across models and domains. records.title: LLMs Infer Cultural Context but Fail to Apply It When Responding
records.summary: Recent work has shown that LLMs overrepresent dominant cultures, particularly Western ones, while marginalizing others. We investigate whether this affects models' ability to generate culturally adapted responses by evaluating their use of local measurement units based on the user's perceived cultural background. We introduce Cultural and Pragmatic Response Inference (CAPRI), a dataset of conversations with varying levels of cultural cues. records.title: Identifying Effective Strategies in Prompt Evolution for Stress and Emotion Prediction
records.summary: Early stress detection and risk prediction are crucial for timely mental health assessment and support. While large language models have recently shown promise for social media stress prediction, relying on accuracy can obscure false positives. Also, prompt revisions yield inconsistent gains across models and tasks, with unclear links to strategy combinations and instruction changes. records.title: Jev for Scientific Decisions: Evaluating Semantic Choices and Their Consequences
records.summary: Scientific workflows often require choosing among known relations before a deterministic calculation can proceed. Whether observations share a culture, treatment or reference standard can change the scientific meaning of the resulting count or comparison. We evaluate Jev as a semantic decision component using a harness that follows its documented guidance and assigns arithmetic to code. The study compares twelve model configurations on twenty source-grounded Choices across ten scientific cases, each repeated five times. records.title: Calibration Language Shapes Block-Influence Pruning in Multilingual Language Models
records.summary: Block Influence (BI) ranks Transformer blocks for depth pruning from their input-output cosine change, but the ranking depends on the calibration distribution. We study whether English calibration transfers to Indian languages in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B, and Gemma-2-2B. records.title: DPA-MoE: A Runtime Precision Control Framework for MoE Inference
records.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation by routing each token to a small set of experts, but each selected expert is still used at a fixed precision. We present DPA-MoE, a runtime precision control framework that makes routed experts any-precision. DPA-MoE encodes expert feed-forward weights as prefix-decodable chunks using SharedScale AnyBCQ, profiles per-expert reconstruction residuals offline, and allocates chunks at inference time using live router gate scores. This post-routing allocation lets a single encoded MoE checkpoint operate at multiple effective weight budgets without retraining or re-encoding. records.title: ESG-Kor: A Korean Dataset for ESG-related Information Extraction and Practical Use Cases
records.summary: With the expansion of pre-trained language model usage in recent years, the importance of datasets for performing tasks in specialized domains has significantly increased. Therefore, we have built a Korean dataset called ESG-Kor to automatically extract Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information, which has recently gained importance. ESG-Kor is a dataset consisting of a total of 118,946 sentences that extracted information on each ESG component from Korean companies' sustainability reports and manually labeled it according to objective rules provided by ESG evaluation agencies. records.title: RenoLayout: Unified Floorplan Renovation and Furniture Layout for Constraint-Aware Residential Design
records.summary: Residential design aims to transform existing homes into functional living spaces while satisfying diverse design preferences and physical constraints. However, existing floorplan generation methods typically assume empty building boundaries as input, whereas renovation requires reasoning over existing floorplans. Furthermore, floorplan renovation and furniture layout are commonly addressed as separate tasks, overlooking their inherent spatial dependency. Consequently, practical residential design must preserve immutable structural components while transforming editable spatial elements. records.title: Embeddings Are Overpriced? A Frozen 16 MB Vocabulary for Small and Ternary Language Models
records.summary: In a small language model the vocabulary is the single largest part. In Gemma 3 270M the embedding table holds 168M of 268M parameters, and because quantisation methods leave the embedding in 16-bit, it is also most of the file once the rest of the model is compressed. We ask what that table actually buys. We replace it with one frozen table of 512-bit codes, 16 MB, with no trainable parameters, derived once from a pretrained embedding by principal-component projection and sign binarisation, and we train the same Gemma-shaped body from scratch on the same 2.05B tokens with and without it. records.title: Emotion Is Not External Knowledge: Internal Attention Signals for Affective State Reasoning
records.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly operate in multi-turn interactions that require maintaining latent conversational states, not only explicit facts. We study affective state as an implicit state inferred from sparse contextual cues that remain relevant after topic shifts, and ask whether LLMs expose internal attention signals for routing such evidence at inference time. Prior attention interventions rely on labeled in-domain head profiles and externally specified target spans, limiting transfer across affective-evidence distributions. records.title: OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering
records.summary: Agentic knowledge graph question answering(KGQA) relies on sequences of executable operations, but trajectory-level rewards obscure their individual contributions. records.title: Ranking and Partitioning of Attention Heads for Sparse and Continual Reinforcement Learning Fine-tuning
records.summary: We study sparse and continual reinforcement learning fine-tuning of language models through attention-head ranking and partitioning. For sparse learning, we rank attention heads by gradient norm to identify a small subset of heads that can be trained effectively. For continual learning, we partition heads across tasks to reduce cross-task interference and preserve previously learned capabilities. records.title: VoteGEO-Bench: Measuring the Impact of Generative Engine Optimization on Electoral Visibility
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for election information, yet little is known about how external web content shapes the political information they present. Generative engine optimization (GEO) rewrites web content to improve its visibility in generated responses. To investigate its potential risks in voting scenarios (VoteGEO), we introduce VoteGEO-Bench, a benchmark covering the 2024 U.S. presidential election and the 2026 Japanese House of Representatives election, combining election-related queries, historical webpages, and voter personas. records.title: Hybrid Generative-Tagging Decoding for Efficient Product Attribute-Value Extraction
records.summary: Attribute-value extraction is important for building high-quality product catalogs in e-commerce. Existing systems either rely on generative or tagging strategies for extracting the attribute names and their corresponding values. Tagging models directly label spans in the source, making them fast and grounded, but they cannot produce values that require reformatting or generate rare attribute names outside their label space. Generative models avoid these drawbacks by generating both attribute names and values token by token, but this auto-regressive nature makes them slow and limits attribute coverage. records.title: DocPilot: Interactive Agent Orchestration and Training for Long Visual Document Understanding
records.summary: Multimodal long-document question answering requires models to seek sparse evidence across pages and modalities, understand heterogeneous document content, and reason over the collected evidence. Even advanced vision-language models (VLMs) can overlook sparse evidence and struggle with cross-modal reasoning in a single pass. Existing document agents further introduce multi-step interaction, but some still rely on predefined workflows or coarse-grained actions, limiting the flexibility and granularity of document reasoning. records.title: ZoomCap: Evidence-Routed Visual Zooming for Recoverable Visual Information Transfer
records.summary: Detailed captions transfer visual information into vision-language model supervision, but quality is easily conflated with length: long single-pass outputs still miss small objects, text, and spatial relations or promote uncertain observations into confident claims. We formulate fine-grained captioning as recoverable visual information transfer, in which a teacher acquires missing evidence under a finite observation budget and converts it into reusable supervision. records.title: JetSpec++: Foresight Parallel Drafting with Self Refinements
records.summary: Speculative decoding's effectiveness is governed by two quantities: the acceptance rate of drafted tokens and the cost of producing them. records.title: PocketTSLM: Deploying an On-Device Soft-Prompt Time-Series Language Model for Privacy-Preserving Smartphone Reasoning
records.summary: Consumer phones and wearables increasingly collect physiological time-series data, yet most mobile systems treat these streams as summaries or text rather than as temporal evidence. This representation is poorly matched to personal health systems that need to retrieve, route, or summarize sensor evidence while preserving temporal structure. Cloud-hosted time-series language models avoid smartphone limits, but they repeatedly move sensitive physiology off the device and add latency and per-query compute cost. records.title: VALCON: Benchmarking and Enhancing Value Consistency in Large Language Models via Dual-Role Variation
records.summary: Current value alignment evaluations for large language models (LLMs) heavily rely on output compliance, overlooking whether LLMs maintain value consistency when alternating between generator and evaluator roles. Such consistency is increasingly important because modern LLM agents and alignment pipelines often rely on the same LLM to both generate actions and evaluate their acceptability. To mitigate this limitation, we propose VALCON, a role-driven data construction framework that operationalizes value consistency into three benchmark suites (VAB-Consistency, VAB-Boundary, VAB-Challenge) via dual-role variation. records.title: Making every stage of medical device document assessment with large language models deterministic
records.summary: To show that a medical device complies with regulation, experts judge whether documents and records meet each requirement and record the judgment for others to verify. For each assessment item that experts define, large language models could prepare a preliminary assessment: a label such as Satisfied or Not satisfied, a reason and quoted evidence. We sent fourteen commercial deployments of such models (seven models from three providers, through six routes) the same request repeatedly, with the deterministic sampling settings each accepted; every deployment returned differing assessments for at least one request, and in twelve the label changed. records.title: Bias Control and Injection for Multi-Agent Aggregation
records.summary: Multi-agent reasoning with large language models (LLMs) raises a central question for collective decision-making: when agents disagree, whose decision should be trusted? Resolving such disagreements is difficult because agents' decisions are susceptible to non-semantic biases such as majority pressure and response-style preferences, which can obscure the quality of the underlying reasoning. Our analysis shows how bias can be both mitigated and exploited: bias control improves initial answer selection, while bias injection elicits decision instability that serves as a reliability signal. records.title: How Do LLM-Generated Texts Impact Term-Based Retrieval Models?
records.summary: As more content generated by large language models (LLMs) floods into the Internet, information retrieval (IR) systems now face the challenge of distinguishing and handling a blend of human-authored and machine-generated texts. Recent studies suggest that neural retrievers may exhibit a preferential inclination toward LLM-generated content, while classic term-based retrievers like BM25 tend to favor human-written documents. This paper investigates the influence of LLM-generated content on term-based retrieval models, which are valued for their efficiency and robust generalization across domains.
